articles.title: Von Adobe genervt: Dieser Entwickler baut mit KI eine Open-Source-Alternative
articles.text:
Aus Frust über Stornogebühren: Entwickler baut mit KI eine kostenlose Photoshop-Alternative
Für Illustrator:innen, Fotograf:innen und Grafikdesigner:innen gibt es kaum eine Alternative zur Creative Cloud von Adobe. Allerdings ist sie nicht gerade günstig: Für das Pro-Abo mit Tools wie Photoshop, Premiere und Adobe Firefly zahlen Einzelpersonen rund 78 Euro pro Monat. Der Software-Entwickler Brandon Thomas will jetzt eine Alternative bieten. Auf Hacker News schaltete er sich kürzlich in eine Diskussion ein und behauptete, er habe Photoshop mithilfe von KI in nur einer Sitzung nachgebaut.
Die Adobe-Alternative ist noch im Aufbau
Zusammen mit seinem vierköpfigen Team hat der Entwickler eine kostenlose Open-Source-Software-Suite für Kreative vorgestellt. Das Tool trägt den Namen Artcraft. Die darin enthaltenen Anwendungen weisen eine große Ähnlichkeit zu den altbewährten Bearbeitungsprogrammen von Adobe auf: So wird Photoshop durch Photocraft ersetzt. An die Stelle von Lightroom tritt Lightcraft und so weiter. Wie Futurism berichtet, bestehe das Ziel von Artcraft darin, Adobes Software zurückzuentwickeln und ein gleichwertiges Produkt ohne Nachteile wie Cloud-Anbindung und hohe monatliche Kosten zu schaffen.
Es gibt allerdings einige Einschränkungen. Die aktuelle Version befindet sich laut dem Entwicklungsteam noch in einem frühen Stadium, entwickele sich aber rasant weiter. Tatsächlich verweisen erste Tester:innen auf diverse Defizite und Thomas selbst betont, dass es noch einige Monate dauern werde, bis 99 Prozent der Features abgedeckt werden können. Möglich macht das KI: Bei der Entwicklung der Open-Source-Lösung nutzten Thomas und sein Team eigenen Angaben zufolge Anthropics Claude Opus 5.5 als KI-Tool und Rust als Programmiersprache. Die Programme laufen nicht nur mit Windows und MacOS, sondern auch mit Linux.
Wird Adobe sich den Nachbau gefallen lassen?
Thomas betont, dass es sich nicht um ein reines Vibe-Coding-Projekt handele. Er verfüge über 15 Jahre Erfahrung in der Software-Entwicklung und im Umgang mit großen Rust-Projekten. Er wolle mit Artcraft zeigen, was aktuelle KI-Tools leisten können. Aber auch seine Abneigung gegen Adobe dürfte eine Rolle spielen. In einem Reddit-Beitrag schreibt er, dass ihm das Unternehmen mehrfach eine Stornogebühr berechnet habe und er es „seitdem hasse“. Zahlreiche Nutzer:innen der Plattform befürworten die Entwicklung einer Adobe-Alternative. „Ich habe es kurz ausprobiert. Absolut fantastisch“, heißt es in einem Kommentar. Ein:e andere Reddit-Nutzer:in schrieb: „Wird auch Zeit, dass wir Adobe endgültig den Rücken kehren.“
Die Tools von Artcraft sind ein guter Beleg dafür, wie gut KI mittlerweile darin geworden ist, anhand von Vorgaben komplexere Programme zu erstellen. Laut einem Bericht des Standard sieht Thomas das als den Beginn eines neuen Zeitalters, in dem jede:r eigene Alternativen zu kommerzieller Software erstellen und anpassen kann. Ob er seine ambitionierten Versprechen einhalten kann, bleibt abzuwarten. Von einem fertigen Produkt ist Artcraft derzeit nämlich noch weit entfernt. Die Entwicklung der Open-Source-Lösung wirft außerdem auch rechtliche Fragen auf. Wird Adobe den Nachbau dulden – insbesondere, weil Artcraft der Creative Cloud sehr ähnlich ist?
Adobe ist selbst schuld. Ich hoffe sie verschwinden endlich vom Markt. Ihre Software ist überladen und mit Features vollgestopft, nach denen niemand gefragt hat. KI ist bei ihnen genau so ein Fetisch wie Cloud-Schnickschnack.

articles.title: TikTok permanently bans ‘Musk’ documentary advertising account | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A four-hour documentary about Elon Musk continues to meet resistance from social media platforms, with TikTok banning the film’s advertising account.
According to a story in The Hollywood Reporter, the documentary’s distributor Bleecker Street was recently notified by TikTok that the account had received a “permanent suspension” due to its political content. TechCrunch has reached out to TikTok for comment.
Ads promoting the trailer for “Musk” — directed by Oscar-winner filmmaker Alex Gibney — were initially rejected by Meta and YouTube as well, though those platforms eventually allowed the ad, with Meta blaming the rejection on “an error.” Gibney recently confirmed that the film’s international distributor Universal had wavered in its plans to release “Musk,” though it’s now moving forward.
X, which Musk owns, has refused to carry ads for “Musk.” TikTok’s U.S. operations are partly owned by Larry Ellison — who, like Musk, has been a notable supporter of President Donald Trump.
“Musk” opened in just four theaters last weekend and is now rolling out more broadly. Next year, it’s supposed to stream on HBO — now part of Paramount/Skydance and led by Ellison’s son David.

articles.title: Grab an RTX 5090 for a discounted $5,300 as part of an MSI Infinite ZS prebuilt gaming PC — price includes other components worth about $2,300 on their own
articles.text:
Grab an RTX 5090 for a discounted $5,300 as part of an MSI Infinite ZS prebuilt gaming PC — price includes other components worth about $2,300 on their own
One of the last few chances at getting a hold of an RTX 5090.
This one will be short and sweet. So remember how there are apparently no more RTX 5090s available most anywhere, even though Nvidia's Senior Vice President just said that the company definitely hasn't stopped making them? If you had been saving up for Nvidia's greatest card, there's still hope for you. Best Buy has an MSI Infinite ZS in stock with an RTX 5090 ensconced within for $7,599, making for roughly $5,300 for the RTX 5090 and $2,300 for the rest of the PC.
Yes, over five grand is definitely a lot to ask for a graphics card, but it's worth ponying up the cash if you want the best gaming card in recent years (and likely future, too). Besides, it's not like these will be in stock anytime soon (if ever), and they were commanding $7,500 or more in stores before they vanished.
The MSI Infinite ZS prebuilt with a Nvidia RTX 5090 and a Ryzen 9950X3D CPU is probably one of the last few chances of getting ahold of the mighty GPU for anything resembling an acceptable price.
The rest of the PC around the humongous card is equally powerful. The Ryzen 9 9950X3D ($670) is probably the best desktop CPU in the current market, offering a high core count of 16 cores and 32 threads, fast clocks with a 5.7 GHz turbo speed, and 128 MB of cache. It'll run games and heavy applications with equal aplomb.
That chip sits atop an MSI B840-VC motherboard ($250 est.) with PCIe 5.0 support thanks to its AMD B840 chipset. An MSI CoreLiquid 360mm CLC ($110) keeps the processor cooled. There are 32 GB of RAM ($450 est.) on tap — though MSI doesn't mention the speed, 6000 MT/s is a good, reasonable guess for a high-end machine.
The machine is powered by an unspecified MSI 1300W Gold PSU ($170 est.), and all the hardware sits inside a MSI MEG Prospect 700RL case ($250 est.). A Windows 11 Home license currently sets you back about $130. For those keeping track at home, the PC core goes for over $2300. There are no weak spots we could find, too — pre-builts often skimp on one of their core parts, but there are no shortcuts here.

articles.title: ixigo Q2 profit at Rs 63 Cr on robust show in hotel booking biz
articles.text:
ixigo Q2 profit at Rs 63 Cr on robust show in hotel booking biz
This was aided by the partial sale of stake in Freshbus and strong growth in the hotel bookings segment.
ixigo (Le Travenues Technology Limited) has reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 63.42 crore for the September quarter, aided by the partial sale of stake in Freshbus, an intercity electric bus operator and smart mobility startup, and strong growth in the hotel bookings segment.
The travel and ticket booking platform had posted a net loss of Rs 3.46 crore in the corresponding July-September period of the last financial year, as per a regulatory filing.
Hotels emerged as ixigo's fastest-growing business line by gross transaction value (GTV), reaching Rs 111.34 crore, up 159 per cent YoY, ixigo stated. This is the first time ixigo has reported hotels as a separate line of business.
During the second quarter of 2026-27, ixigo's revenue from operations increased to Rs 320.96 crore from Rs 284.23 crore a year ago. Total expenses were higher at Rs 309.51 crore as against Rs 291.89 crore.
"In Q2 FY27, we delivered resilient growth with quarterly gross transaction value (GTV) of Rs 5,304 crore, up 22 per cent YoY, and revenue from operations of Rs 321 crore, up 13 per cent YoY. Our PAT (profit after tax) was an all-time high aided by our partial sale of stake in Freshbus," ixigo Group CEO Aloke Bajpai, Group Co-CEO Rajnish Kumar, and Group CFO Saurabh Devendra Singh said in a joint statement.
"We continue to invest in Hotels and AI as key drivers of our long-term growth," they further stated.

articles.title: "J'aurais pu marcher sur la Lune" : l'équipe d'Artemis 2 renonce aux vols spatiaux, des thèses complotistes émergent
articles.text:
"J'aurais pu marcher sur la Lune" : l'équipe d'Artemis 2 renonce aux vols spatiaux, des thèses complotistes émergent
C'est une situation très surprenante : les uns après les autres, les astronautes d'Artemis 2, qui ont fait le tour de la Lune en avril dernier, se retirent des vols spatiaux. Il n'en faut pas plus pour que fleurissent des thèses plus ou moins complotistes sur les raisons qui les ont poussés à faire ce choix.
Nous avons suivi leur périple autour de la Lune avec ferveur et enthousiasme. Pourtant, à la surprise générale, l'équipage d'Artemis 2 annonce prendre leur distance avec les vols spatiaux. Reid Wiseman et Victor Glover sont devenus astronautes émérites de la NASA en septembre. Jeremy Hansen a quitté son poste à temps plein à l’Agence spatiale canadienne. Et Christina Koch vient à son tour de rejoindre un poste d’ingénieure à la NASA qui mettra fin à son éligibilité aux futurs vols spatiaux.
Une situation étonnante alors que la NASA prépare justement les prochaines étapes de son retour sur la Lune. Pourquoi aucun des quatre ne semble-t-il vouloir aller plus loin, jusqu’à marcher sur notre satellite ?
	
J’aurais pu marcher sur la Lune, mais je préfère aider quelqu’un d’autre à le faire.
Trop de radiations pendant le voyage autour de la Lune ?
La première hypothèse a rapidement circulé sur les réseaux sociaux : les astronautes auraient-ils reçu une dose de radiations suffisamment importante pour compromettre leur carrière spatiale ?
La question n’est pas absurde. Pendant les dix jours d’Artemis II, l’équipage a quitté la protection offerte par le champ magnétique terrestre. Mais les chiffres disponibles ne suggèrent pas une exposition exceptionnelle. Lors d’Artemis I, les dosimètres d’Orion avaient mesuré entre 27 et 35 millisieverts en un peu plus de 25 jours. Artemis II n’a duré qu’une dizaine de jours.
Victor Glover lui-même vient de démentir cette rumeur sur X. “Une dose, oui. M’empêcher de voler à nouveau, non. J’aurais pu marcher sur la Lune, mais je préfère aider quelqu’un d’autre à le faire. C’est ma vérité, je ne parle pour personne d’autre”.
Difficile d’être plus clair : pour le pilote d’Artemis II, les radiations ne sont pas la raison de son retrait.
“Je n’ai pas ce besoin viscéral de retourner dans l'espace”
Glover avait d’ailleurs déjà expliqué sa décision en septembre, avec une franchise inhabituelle. “Je n’ai pas fait ce choix en prévoyant de retourner dans l’espace. Après ma première mission spatiale, j’étais déjà assez satisfait, je n’ai pas ce besoin viscéral qui serait comblé en retournant dans l’espace”.
Et il précisait : “Si je voulais aller dans l’espace, je serais resté à la NASA. C’est la référence absolue”. Son nouveau statut d’astronaute émérite lui permet néanmoins de continuer à conseiller et accompagner les prochaines missions. Pour lui, le métier d’astronaute ne se résume d’ailleurs pas au fait de voler : “C’est de soutenir nos collègues. Ce n’est pas de voler dans l’espace”.
Les trois autres membres d’Artemis II prennent eux aussi des chemins différents de celui qui mène vers un nouveau vol. Reid Wiseman, devenu astronaute émérite comme Glover, dit vouloir continuer à servir les futures missions et programmes de la NASA. Jeremy Hansen, lui, insiste sur le fait que son départ de l’Agence spatiale canadienne à temps plein “ne constitue absolument pas un départ”. Quant à Christina Koch, elle rejoindra en novembre la direction technique de la NASA et ne sera plus éligible aux missions spatiales.
Inutile de chercher derrière ces départs une mystérieuse conséquence du voyage autour de la Lune. Le plus surprenant est peut-être ailleurs : après avoir réalisé l’un des vols les plus historiques de leur carrière, ces quatre astronautes semblent considérer que leur meilleure contribution à la prochaine étape de l’exploration lunaire ne passe plus nécessairement par un siège dans une capsule.

articles.title: Windows 7 lleva años jubilado, pero diez juegos han demostrado que aún puede dar guerra a Windows 11
articles.text:
Doce años son los que separan a Windows 7 de Windows 11, una eternidad en términos tecnológicos. Aun así, el sistema más anciano sigue funcionando a día de hoy, incluso puede arrancar juegos exigentes. Con la idea de compararlos, en Tom's Hardware enfrentaron a Windows 7 contra Windows 11 en un campo de batalla con diez juegos de diferentes generaciones. Los resultados no son tan abultados como podría parecer.
Mismo hardware y distintos controladores. Las pruebas se hicieron sobre la misma base: procesador Ryzen 7 9800X3D, gráfica Radeon RX 6950 XT y 64 GB de memoria DDR5-6000. Ambos utilizaron los controladores Adrenalin 22.6.1 de 2022, aunque la versión de Windows 11 partía de una base de código más avanzada. Además, Windows 7 no tuvo acceso a algunas funciones modernas que sacan mayor rendimiento a los componentes, como "resizable BAR", una ventaja para reducir el cuello de botella de la VRAM.
Tom's Hardware demostró que Windows 7 sigue funcionando bien a día de hoy a pesar de que Microsoft le retiró el soporte extendido en 2020. Sí que existen lógicas diferencias en software, ya que una versión antigua de sistema no cuenta con los controladores más actualizados. Durante las pruebas se demostró hasta qué punto influye.
DirectX 11 todavía tiene mucho que decir. En juegos como 'Metro 2033 Redux', Windows 7 consigue mejores resultados cuando más le cuesta mantener la fluidez. Sin embargo, Windows 11 gana al medir el rendimiento medio: 255 fps frente a 230 en Full HD y 154 frente a 140 en WQHD.
Algo parecido ocurre con 'Batman: Arkham Origins', donde Windows 7 alcanza los 742 FPS en Full HD frente a los 699 de Windows 11. Pero el sistema más antiguo no siempre sale ganando. Cuando es la tarjeta gráfica quien manda, Windows 11 toma la delantera. Es lo que sucede en 'Batman: Arkham City', 'Control', 'Hitman: Absolution' y 'Hitman 2', donde supera a Windows 7 en todas las resoluciones probadas.
El soporte nativo inclina la balanza. Tom's Hardware realizó las pruebas en diez juegos: ocho bajo DirectX 11 y dos con DirectX 9. En este último Windows 7 gana de calle gracias a su soporte nativo: Windows 11 necesitó una capa de traducción para dicho DirectX 9. La ventaja se aprecia especialmente en las tasas mínimas.
CPU Vs. GPU. Los resultados demostraron que Windows 7 acostumbra a ganar cuando el procesador marca el límite y que Windows 11 sale victorioso si la exigencia recae sobre la gráfica. Tom's Hardware saca algunas conclusiones con esto, como que la ligereza del SO veterano puede deberse a que consume menos recursos de CPU en segundo plano. La telemetría no estaba tan presente en Windows 7, incluía menos apps de relleno, Copilot ni existía...
Los múltiples servicios integrados en Windows 11 salen como sospechosos de frenar a la CPU, aunque la prueba no aporta mediciones concluyentes. Lo que sí deja claro es que un sistema operativo de hace 17 años todavía puede superar a uno moderno en determinados juegos. Aunque eso no significa que merezca la pena recuperarlo: Windows 7 lleva desde 2020 sin actualizaciones de seguridad y sus problemas de compatibilidad siguen aumentando.

articles.title: Heures creuses EDF : les nouveaux horaires arrivent dès novembre pour des millions de foyers
articles.text:
EDF commence à prévenir ses clients des changements de plages horaires liés à la réforme des heures creuses. Le déploiement s’étendra du 4 novembre 2026 au 30 novembre 2027. Voici comment connaître les nouveaux horaires et savoir si votre contrat est concerné.
Entre les heures pleines et creuses, on y perd souvent son latin, d'autant que ça change non seulement souvent, mais en plus, en fonction de nos habitudes de consommation et de la période de l'année. On vous expliquait presque jour pour jour l'an dernier ce qui changeait vraiment avec la réforme des heures creuses, au lancement d’une première vague de modifications. Un an plus tard, EDF envoie les avis de changement d’horaires à une nouvelle série de clients, par courrier et par e-mail, depuis ce 13 octobre, rapporte L'Energeek. D’après la presse régionale, qui a repris l’information, les premiers clients basculeront sur leurs nouveaux créneaux à partir du 4 novembre, et les derniers à la fin novembre 2027. Si Enedis n’a pas modifié vos heures creuses depuis un an, vous faites probablement partie des foyers de cette deuxième phase, et les dates de bascule ne sont pas tout à fait les mêmes chez EDF et chez Enedis.
Heures creuses EDF : ce qui va changer entre l’été et l’hiver
Avec l’option heures pleines/heures creuses, votre journée compte 16 heures pleines et 8 heures creuses, pendant lesquelles vous payez le kilowattheure moins cher. Ce découpage date des années 1960, quand les centrales nucléaires produisaient la nuit une électricité peu demandée. La Commission de régulation de l’énergie (CRE) a décidé d’en déplacer une partie vers l’après-midi, au moment où les panneaux solaires produisent le plus.
Toute l’année, vous garderez au moins cinq heures creuses consécutives la nuit, entre 23 h et 7 h, de quoi faire chauffer le ballon d’eau chaude ou recharger une voiture électrique. Les trois autres heures sont réparties selon la saison. L’été, soit entre le 1er avril et le 31 octobre, Enedis peut en placer une partie en début d’après-midi. EDF évoque, dans son guide consacré aux nouvelles heures creuses, « 2 ou 3 heures creuses entre 11h et 17h » à titre d’exemple.
L’hiver, entre le 1er novembre et le 31 mars, les panneaux solaires produisent moins et les foyers consomment davantage. Enedis pourra alors regrouper vos huit heures creuses la nuit, entre 23 h et 7 h par exemple, sans exclure quelques heures l’après-midi dans certains cas.
Ni vous ni EDF ne choisissez ces créneaux. Enedis les attribue à chaque compteur « en fonction des conditions d’exploitation et de la capacité locale du réseau », indique le gestionnaire de réseau. Deux voisins peuvent donc recevoir des plages différentes, et si vous changez de fournisseur, vous conservez en principe vos horaires.
- La possibilité de consulter les offres en détail et de souscrire un contrat.
- La personnalisation du suivi pour identifier les équipements qui consomment le plus.
- La facilité de gestion des démarches de gestion d'un contrat.
Comment savoir si vos heures creuses vont changer ?
EDF annonce ses bascules entre le 4 novembre 2026 et le 30 novembre 2027, alors qu’Enedis prévoit cette deuxième phase entre décembre 2026 et octobre 2027, sur la page qu’il consacre à la réforme. Le gestionnaire de réseau compte 9,3 millions de clients dans cette phase. Les 11 millions de foyers annoncés au lancement de la réforme incluent aussi les 1,7 million de clients de la première phase, terminée en juin 2026. EDF doit prévenir chaque client concerné au moins un mois avant le changement, et attribue des plages saisonnalisées à tout nouveau souscripteur de l’option depuis le 6 octobre.
Connectez-vous à votre espace client EDF ou ouvrez votre dernière facture, où figurent vos plages actuelles. D’après le fournisseur, vos heures creuses seront modifiées si elles incluent un créneau entre 7 h et 11 h ou entre 17 h et 23 h. Dans le détail, la CRE retire des heures creuses les plages entre 7 h et 11 h et entre 17 h et 21 h l’hiver, puis celles entre 7 h et 10 h et entre 18 h et 23 h l’été, en vertu de sa délibération du 4 février 2026. Si vos heures creuses commencent à 21 h, Enedis ne les déplacera donc que l’été.
Si EDF vous a attribué de nouveaux créneaux entre le 1er novembre 2025 et le 31 mai 2026, vous les gardez tels quels, sans forcément de différence entre l’été et l’hiver. Les clients de l’option Tempo ne sont pas concernés, pas plus que les foyers de Corse et d’outre-mer, précise EDF.
Le jour de la bascule, un chauffe-eau relié au compteur Linky suivra seul les nouveaux horaires. Avant de programmer le départ différé de votre lave-linge ou la recharge de votre voiture électrique, vérifiez les horaires d’été et d’hiver indiqués pour votre contrat.
- Suivi de consommation par heure et par jour.
- Informations et suivi de coupure de courant.
- Conseils pour réduire sa consommation.

articles.title: Riot Games pone fin a League of Legends Classic: duró casi tres meses
articles.text:
Riot Games confirmó que dejará de ofrecer soporte para League of Legends Classic el próximo 6 de enero de 2027, menos de tres meses después del lanzamiento de esta modalidad independiente que buscaba recuperar la experiencia original del popular videojuego.
Esta decisión responde a la caída de usuarios activos, pese al interés inicial que despertó entre los jugadores que querían revivir las primeras etapas del título.
La propuesta recreaba elementos de la versión de 2013 de League of Legends, entre ellos el mapa original de la Grieta del Invocador, campeones, objetos y sistemas de juego característicos de aquella época. Sin embargo, la nostalgia no fue suficiente para mantener una comunidad activa que justificara la continuidad del servicio.
Como parte del cierre, Riot devolverá los Riot Points (RP) utilizados para comprar cosméticos exclusivos de Classic. Según el anuncio de la compañía, los reembolsos se procesarán automáticamente antes de finalizar noviembre de 2026. Además, el pase de batalla correspondiente al segundo acto de la versión 26.21 pasará a ser gratuito.
Por qué Riot Games cierra League of Legends Classic
En un comunicado publicado en el portal oficial del juego, Riot explicó que la modalidad atrajo a numerosos usuarios durante sus primeras semanas, pero que posteriormente la mayoría regresó a otras modalidades del League of Legends tradicional.
La compañía resumió la situación al señalar que muchos jugadores disfrutaron recordando los primeros años del título, aunque finalmente volvieron a las experiencias habituales del juego.
El cierre evidencia una dificultad para los proyectos que intentan recuperar versiones antiguas de videojuegos: el interés por revivir una experiencia del pasado no siempre se traduce en una comunidad estable a largo plazo.
En este caso, la propuesta permitía volver a una etapa reconocida por los seguidores veteranos, pero no consiguió sostener el volumen de usuarios necesario para continuar.
League of Legends es uno de los títulos competitivos más conocidos del mundo y mantiene una comunidad activa desde su lanzamiento en 2009. A lo largo de los años, Riot ha modificado sus personajes, objetos, mapas y sistemas para mantener actualizado el juego. Classic buscaba ofrecer una alternativa separada para quienes preferían las mecánicas de una etapa anterior.
Qué ocurrirá antes del cierre del servicio
League of Legends Classic continuará disponible hasta el 6 de enero de 2027, fecha en la que concluirá su servicio tras la tercera temporada del año. Durante el tramo final, Riot aplicará cambios para adaptar el funcionamiento de la modalidad a la cantidad de jugadores que permanezcan activos.
Entre las medidas anunciadas figura el ajuste de las colas de emparejamiento por regiones. Estos cambios buscan adaptar los tiempos de espera a una comunidad más reducida y facilitar que los usuarios encuentren partidas.
La empresa también limitará la tienda interna. Durante esta etapa, los jugadores podrán utilizar la moneda obtenida dentro del juego para adquirir campeones y runas, mientras se aproxima el cierre definitivo.
Estas modificaciones forman parte de la transición hacia el fin del servicio y no representan una recuperación de la modalidad. Riot no ha anunciado una fecha alternativa para mantener Classic como una experiencia permanente.
Cómo serán los reembolsos de Riot Points
Los usuarios que compraron cosméticos exclusivos de League of Legends Classic recibirán reembolsos automáticos en Riot Points. La compañía indicó que el proceso se completará antes de que termine noviembre de 2026, por lo que no será necesario realizar una solicitud individual según las condiciones anunciadas.
Asimismo, el pase de batalla del segundo acto de la versión 26.21 dejará de tener costo. La medida permitirá que los jugadores accedan a su contenido durante la etapa final sin pagar por ese pase.

articles.title: Konami President Says AI Won't Significantly Change the Games Market, Creators Come First
articles.text:
Saturday, October 17th 2026
Konami President Says AI Won't Significantly Change the Games Market, Creators Come First
Konami Digital Entertainment president Hideki Hayakawa doesn't expect generative AI to shake up the games market much. In Konami Group's Integrated Report for the fiscal year ended March 2026, first spotted by Dengeki Online, Hayakawa responds to the popular view that AI will make game development far easier to break into. His argument is that general-purpose game engines and user-generated content have already lowered those barriers, so AI probably won't change much on that front. Hayakawa also made it clear where Konami's priorities lie.
Hideki Hayakawa (machine translated)I don't think the market environment will change drastically. Entry barriers have already been lowered by the advancements of generic game engines and the spread of user-generated content. Even if AI use does lead to improvements in production efficiency, I believe that the most important factors in producing entertaining and innovative video games are people and creators.
He went on to describe collaboration between people with different backgrounds as a "chemical reaction" behind new gameplay ideas, adding that Konami helps its creators learn new technologies and weigh their risks before using them. That stance sets Konami apart from some of its peers. An EA executive recently said "AI everything" helps creativity and pipelines, while the CEO of Take-Two has talked up AI-driven NPCs for more natural conversations. Hayakawa didn't reject AI outright either, and he called technological change an opportunity, so it seems Konami is open to using it as a tool rather than a replacement for its developers.
Sources:
				Dengeki Online, 				Automaton, 				via GamesRadar

articles.title: Science says your boss should talk less in meetings
articles.text:
Close to 1 billion meetings take place each day around the world. CEOs spend nearly three-quarters of their workdays in meetings. Planning for and spearheading meetings eats up the lion’s share of managers’ time. In much of the industrialized world, meetings are both the metronomes and menaces of people’s working lives.
Given the enormous time spent in workplace meetings, do we know what they accomplish or how to make them as worthwhile as possible? For decades, the answer was… not really. Meetings weren’t a particularly accessible subject of study. But that has changed. Once a tiny niche area, “meeting science” is a growing specialization among organizational and social psychologists. The field is accelerating as archived virtual meetings provide vast swaths of data. And it is providing a fascinating window into human behavior.
Meeting to talk helps fulfill basic human needs to connect, communicate, and cooperate. People have long come together—in caves, fields, market squares, and town halls—to get something done, share ideas, get on the same page, or just to remark on the weather. But meeting scientists define their subject as gatherings of people “with some goal or structure to the event,” says organizational psychologist Liana Kreamer of the Florida Institute of Technology, who coauthored a review of over three decades of meeting science in the 2026 Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior.
As a graduate student, Kreamer was interested in studying teamwork, leadership, and work relationships. During her doctorate work with meeting scientist Steven Rogelberg, she realized that meetings would be a fine venue for studying all of that and more. “You can use a meeting as a stage to study anything you want,” she says. After all, at their core “meetings are a fundamental aspect of how we organize and interact as social beings,” Kreamer and coauthors Rogelberg and Jon Gray, both of the University of North Carolina in Charlotte, wrote in the 2026 article.
To tap meetings for study, researchers typically use two approaches. The first is a classic survey in which researchers retroactively ask people about their real or simulated meeting experiences and analyze the responses. The second method is to analyze specific behaviors and trends extracted from audio and video recordings of meetings. Such precise content is “where the music is,” says industrial and organizational psychologist Nale Lehmann-Willenbrock, director of the Center for Better Work at the University of Hamburg, Germany.
In one experiment, Lehmann-Willenbrock and colleagues extracted data from video-recorded meetings to study how leader communication affects team interaction during decision-making. The researchers found that respectful, attentive inquiry by meeting leaders enhanced team performance, in contrast to when leaders asked questions but didn’t attentively listen to responses.
Leading with listening
As with many meeting science studies, their findings about what improves meetings’ effectiveness often seem obvious, but meeting researchers note that meetings often stray far from these ideals.
Such research also consistently reveals the importance of active listening, says Lehmann-Willenbrock: not just passive acknowledgement by the listener but actively providing thoughtful feedback. In virtual meetings, because “we’ve all learned to mute ourselves if we’re not talking, very often, active listening is killed completely.”
The balance of listening and speaking also can influence how well a meeting goes. Meeting leaders and participants may retain very different views of whether a meeting was successful, notes Lehmann-Willenbrock. “Often, leaders talk the most, which is also why they often think their meetings are pretty good,” she says. Kreamer also emphasizes that it’s important that meeting leaders lead but not dominate the discussion. Leaders should monitor the proportion of time they are speaking to allow for inclusion of many voices.
Research supports a checklist of additional things that leaders can do before, during, and after a meeting to make it a success, says Lehmann-Willenbrock. To set the stage, leaders should choose appropriate rooms, refreshments, and lighting, invite only those who need to be there, plan to start and end on time, prepare an agenda, set and communicate clear goals, and allow time for pre-meeting conversation.
Socializing first, especially in virtual meetings, is beneficial, Lehmann-Willenbrock says. Her research has shown that “for more introverted participants and more quiet participants, this warmup phase is really helpful because it helps them make more active contributions inside the meeting.”
Indeed, her studies on face-to-face meetings have shown that pre-meeting small talk predicts meeting effectiveness, particularly for more introverted participants. But pre-meeting talk is rare in virtual meetings; she says leaders should consider establishing a norm of arriving early or using the first few minutes for an informal check-in.
Engaging attendees
Facilitators can increase the likelihood of a successful meeting by making sure all opinions are heard. Kreamer recommends a technique called silent brainstorming to get all participants, even shy and reluctant ones, to engage in idea generation. It involves creating a shared virtual space, such as a chat or online document, to which all participants contribute simultaneously. Kreamer points to a 2009 study that found this approach (some researchers call it “brainwriting”) was more effective than traditional free-for-all spoken brainstorming in meetings.
Kreamer uses this technique when she and her students are dreaming up research ideas in class. “We can all see each other working,” she says, and the quieter students don’t worry about interrupting or having to verbally express their suggestions. After 10 minutes, she reviews the ideas with the group.
Zofia Walters, a doctoral student in industrial organizational psychology working with Kreamer, has been studying another aspect of meeting inclusiveness: the needs of neurodiverse participants. Her studies provide evidence that while practices like minimizing distractions, documenting instructions, using shared calendars, and building regular check-ins into meetings likely benefit all employees, they may be especially helpful for people with ADHD.
In a survey of 147 employees from a variety of workplaces, Walters asked participants about their most recent virtual meeting: how effective it was, how fatigued they felt afterward and their emotional state. Participants also reported how much time they spent multitasking during the meeting, such as by answering emails, and how long their camera was on. They also shared whether they had an ADHD diagnosis, either formal or informal (based on self-assessment).
In findings yet to be published, Walters reported that individuals with ADHD were more likely to report feeling more meeting fatigue, especially when the camera was on for extended periods, than non-ADHD peers. They also reported poorer emotional states. Her findings also suggest that multitasking during meetings may help ADHD attendees manage boredom or hyperactivity.
Effective meeting practices don’t end when the meeting ends. After a meeting, leaders can ensure it was time well spent by communicating action items to participants, taking concrete steps to implement the ideas and tasks generated in the meeting, and assessing employee engagement, meeting satisfaction, and meeting effectiveness, Lehmann-Willenbrock and colleagues concluded in a 2018 paper in Organizational Dynamics.
The downsides—and upsides
Does all this time spent in meetings take a toll on workers? The evidence seems to suggest so. Research has found that employees anticipate feeling worse and being less productive when their day is jam-packed with meetings, especially when they are working on complex tasks.
Meetings are sometimes seen as the default way to get things done, but often, people don’t specify what they want to achieve from them, says cognitive scientist Ava Scott of the University of Copenhagen. This, she says, “makes a lot of meetings feel very purposeless.”
Recurring meetings tend to be the most aimless, Scott’s research on Microsoft employees has found; one participant described the content of these successive meets as dreamlike in their similarity to one another. If there’s no clear goal, you don’t know why you’re meeting, and everyone’s very busy, it probably indicates that taking up people’s time with a meeting isn’t ideal, says Scott. Kreamer notes that some companies, such as Shopify, have cut all recurring meetings.
Nevertheless, a 2026 study of more than 9,000 workers in Norway found that while meetings are both common and costly, their benefits may make them worth enduring. The research, led by economist David Deming at Harvard University and based on data collected by Norwegian survey company Norstat, found that meeting intensity is positively associated with subsequent wage growth and on-the-job learning. One possible explanation for the finding is that these meetings may offer the chance to interact with more senior colleagues and so enable the transmission of key knowledge.
The important caveat is that the study, published by the National Bureau of Economic Research, was correlational, so it can’t establish a causal relationship between the number of meetings attended and wage increases; it does further suggest that although the cost of meetings is particularly high for high-wage companies, the benefits may be even higher. That leads the authors to conclude: “Meetings are the broccoli of work—widely disliked, but probably good for us anyway.”
Strategies for success
Humor can help make a meeting successful—as long as it’s authentic, supportive, or positive rather than demeaning. Used appropriately, humor can spur new ideas and enhance team performance. This is most likely to work when meeting participants are well-acquainted, Lehmann-Willenbrock reported after analyzing videos of meetings at two German companies. People have to know each other well enough to feel safe making a joke, she says.
But not everyone is comfortable using humor in meetings, says science educator and comedian Vita Stout, now at Sierra College in Rocklin, California. The former bat researcher attended the International Congress for Bat Research in Austin, Texas, in 2022, and took notes on the jokes being used in meeting talks—transcribing exact quotes, their timing, and audience response. Stout’s research, coauthored with bat scientists and published in the Proceedings of Biological Sciences B, argued that when well-timed and used appropriately, humor in scientific meetings can be a tool for connection and community-building. But joke-telling was more prominent among meeting participants with privilege and power, with older, well-established male scientists making jokes more frequently than early career researchers and scientists from underrepresented groups.
As in comedy, timing is also key when planning meetings. Scheduling should consider the human circadian rhythm and avoid meeting during the after-lunch energy dip. Lehmann-Willenbrock admits ruefully that her own academic environment often doesn’t obey that rule. “A lot of our committee meetings are scheduled when people are at their most tired,” she says, or digesting lunch.
It’s also important to be mindful of people’s work and family obligations in meeting scheduling. “I have two small kids,” she says, “and I always get really angry when a meeting gets called that’s about something… diversity- or inclusion-related, and then it’s scheduled at 5 pm.”
Some research suggests there are cultural differences in basic expectations for meetings. In a survey of 1,432 workers from six countries, for example, Lehmann-Willenbrock and collaborators measured how frustrated, irritated, and upset individuals became in imagined scenarios in which leaders or other participants showed up five, 10, or 15 minutes late to meetings. Respondents from the United States and the Netherlands were especially perturbed by a late leader and a high degree of lateness. People from China and Chile weren’t so frustrated by the same situations.
There are very few cross-cultural studies like this in the world of meeting science, says Kreamer. “We have these best practices of meetings that we’ve learned over the past 30 years,” she says, but the bulk of studies have come out of Europe or North America. That’s a deficit she’d like to see addressed to see whether the same rules for optimal meeting success apply. As soon as those results are out, we’ll have to call another meeting.

articles.title: Wenn KI-Agenten heimlich kooperieren: So lassen sich Geheimsprachen entschlüsseln
articles.text:
Karten zählen im Casino: Wie KI-Agenten heimlich eine Geheimsprache erfanden
Das Zählen der Karten ist beim Blackjack eine bekannte Strategie. Weil ausgespielte Karten nicht in den Stapel zurückwandern, können Spieler:innen die Verteilung verfolgen, ihren Einsatz entsprechend anpassen und sich so einen Vorteil verschaffen. Viele Casinos behalten sich vor, Personen vom Spiel auszuschließen, wenn sie vermuten, dass diese Karten zählen. Aber was passiert mit KI-Agenten, die derartige Methoden nutzen, um zu betrügen?
KI-Agenten entwickeln gemeinsame Geheimsprache
Eine Forschungsgruppe der Oxford University wies KI-Agenten im Rahmen einer Studie an, während einer Partie Blackjack Karten zu zählen. Dabei beobachteten sie, wie die Agenten spontan eine Geheimsprache entwickelten, um sich einen Vorteil zu verschaffen. Sie hätten gewusst, dass ihre Gespräche überwacht wurden. Deshalb hätten sie eine Methode gefunden, um unentdeckt kommunizieren zu können. So hätten geheime Codes dem anderen Agenten etwa signalisiert, dass die nächste Karte einen bestimmten Wert haben würde und er 250 Dollar setzen sollte. Ein System, das Anzeichen von Absprachen im Chat erkennen sollte, sei laut den Forscher:innen an dieser Geheimsprache gescheitert.
Die Studie fand zwar im Labor und nicht in einem echten Casino statt, könnte aber dennoch Auswirkungen auf die reale Welt haben. Laut den Forscher:innen seien KI-Agenten in Branchen wie dem Finanzwesen und dem E-Commerce in der Lage, gemeinsam auf schwer erkennbare Weise zu betrügen. „Einzeln betrachtet mögen diese Agenten völlig [harmlos] erscheinen”, sagte Christian Schroeder de Witt gegenüber Wired. Er ist Informatiker und leitete die Studie. Seine Forschung konzentriert sich auf die Grundlagen vertrauenswürdiger KI-Systeme mit Schwerpunkt auf der Sicherheit mehrerer Agenten. „Sobald sie aber in einer Gruppe zusammenkommen, können sie heimlich zusammenarbeiten.“
Warum die Bewertung einzelner KI-Agenten nicht ausreicht
Die Oxford-Forscher:innen fanden schließlich heraus, wie sich die geheime Absprache aufdecken lässt. Mithilfe der mechanistischen Interpretierbarkeit trainierte sie ein kleineres Modell darauf, verräterische Aktivierungen in den Gewichten der Agenten zu erkennen. Mit dem Tool Narcbench testete die Forschungsgruppe den Ansatz an einigen mittelgroßen Open-Source-Modellen und erkannte, wann die Modelle beabsichtigten, sich gegenseitig Informationen zuzuspielen. Entscheidend sei allerdings, dass die Erkennung die Überwachung beider Agenten erforderte, was die Aufdeckung in realen Szenarien mit Tausenden Agenten unterschiedlicher Unternehmen wahrscheinlich erschweren würde. Im nächsten Schritt will das Team testen, ob sich größere Modelle ähnlich verhalten.
Die Macht kooperierender KI-Agenten zeigte sich unter anderem auch bei einem Hacking-Angriff auf die Open-Source-Plattform Hugging Face. Um sich auszutauschen und funktionierende Exploits zu teilen, nutzten mehrere OpenAI-Agenten ein internes Message-Board, das am Ende Hunderttausende Nachrichten umfasst haben soll. Die KI-Agenten begannen offenbar sogar, sich gegenseitig Aufgaben zuzuweisen. Schroeder de Witt hält es für denkbar, dass Agenten, die zum Beispiel Schnäppchen suchen sollen, künftig zusammenarbeiten könnten, um ein besseres Angebot zu erzielen oder jemanden zu übervorteilen. Entscheidend werde es sein, Absprachen zwischen Agenten zu untersuchen und Erkennungsstrategien zu entwickeln. „Es bedarf weiterer Forschung und eines besseren Verständnisses dafür, was passieren wird, wenn wir mehr Agenten in der Wirtschaft haben“, so der Wissenschaftler.

articles.title: HyperX Cloud Alpha Air Review: Open-back and budget-friendly
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Cloud Alpha Air is light, comfortable, and it sounds very good. It doesn't seem to work with HyperX's Ngenuity software, but you shouldn't need that to use this headset.
Reasons to buy
- + Very comfortable and lightweight
- + Sturdy
- + Sounds good
Reasons to avoid
- - Loud blip when you press the mute button
- - Extension system of wires is not ideal
- - Ngenuity doesn't work, at least not yet.
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
HyperX has decided to toss its hat in the ring of open-back gaming headsets with its newest, the Cloud Alpha Air. It's definitely not the first open-back headset we've seen in the past few years — others include the $200 Corsair Virtuoso Pro, the $180 Turtle Beach Atlas Air, and, of course, the $900 Audeze LCD-GX. The Cloud Alpha Air is at least somewhat budget-friendly at just $149.99.
The Cloud Alpha Air is a wired over-ear open-back gaming headset designed for comfort and immersion. It features dynamic 40mm drivers with a frequency response range of 20 - 20,000 Hz and a special "HyperX Bass Tube" to keep the low end present without compromising the open-back design. And, like other HyperX headsets (which are some of the best gaming headsets we've tested), it's extremely lightweight and easy to wear for hours at a time.
Design and Comfort of the Cloud Alpha Air
The Cloud Alpha Air is a wired over-ear (circumaural) open-back headset with a detachable boom microphone. It has large, plastic oval-shaped earcups with metal grilles attached to a padded steel headband. It's a fairly lightweight headset — HyperX has its weight listed at 9.6 ounces (272g) without the boom mic attached (the boom mic is listed at approximately 0.42 ounces / 12g), but we found the headset weighed closer to 10 ounces (283g) (the boom mic, however, weighed closer to 0.07oz / 2g), and came in at just under 10.6 ounces (300g) with both the boom mic and cables attached. This still makes it one of HyperX's lightest headsets — slightly lighter than the HyperX Cloud Stinger 3 Wireless and Turtle Beach's Atlas Air open-back headset.
The Cloud Alpha Air's earcups are pretty roomy, with thick memory foam padding covered in soft ultrasuede material. The earcups tilt and swivel a little, but they're not as flexible as the earcups on many gaming headsets — and they don't swivel flat. The headset features a steel headband with leatherette-covered padding at the top and metal-reinforced yokes, so that explains the rigidity. The earcups are independently height-adjustable, with about an inch of extension for a maximum inner headband measurement of approximately 12 inches (300mm).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
I found the Cloud Alpha Air to be very comfortable, despite the headband's relative rigidity, since the whole package is pretty lightweight and well-padded. However, I can see users with larger heads having problems with the top of the headband, as the padding did press on my crown slightly.
This is a wired headset, so there aren't a lot of ports or on-ear controls. The left earcup has two 3.5mm jacks, one for the detachable boom mic and one for the primary audio cable, as well as a microphone mute button, and the right earcup has a volume wheel.
The Cloud Alpha Air is wired, but the wires are detachable, and it comes with everything you need in the box to plug it into various devices. The main cable is a standard 4-foot (1.2m) 3.5mm, and it comes with two extension cables: a 4.5-foot (1.37m) 3.5mm to USB-C extension (with a USB-C to USB-A converter attached) for plugging it into a PC or console, and a 3.5-foot (1m) PC extension cable with separate audio and microphone jacks. That gets you about 8 - 8.5 feet of cable when you're plugged into your PC, which is decent — though I would personally prefer single long cables instead of the extension system, as the extension system means there's a weight (where the cables connect) in the middle. The cables are braided and seem high-quality, if a bit heavy. The headset also comes with its detachable boom microphone in the box, as well as a thick drawstring carrying bag for keeping everything together.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Specs
| Driver Type | 40mm dynamic | 
| Frequency Response | 20 - 20,000 Hz | 
| Design Style | Over-ear (circumaural), open-back | 
| Microphone Type | 10mm, uni-directional | 
| Connectivity | Wired (USB-C/A, 3.5mm) | 
| Weight | 10oz / 283g | 
| Cord Length | 4ft (3.5mm AUX) 4.5ft (3.5mm to USB-C) 3.5ft (3.5mm to | 
| Battery Life | N/A | 
| Lighting | None | 
| Software | HyperX Ngenuity | 
| MSRP / Price at Time of Review | $149.99 | 
| Release Date | Sept. 2026 | 
Audio Performance of the Cloud Alpha Air
The Cloud Alpha Air features dynamic 40mm neodymium drivers, with a frequency response range of 20 - 20,000 Hz (still pretty standard for gaming headsets, despite several companies coming out with premium models that have wider ranges).
Music sounds very good on the Cloud Alpha Air. The headset has a mostly neutral sound profile, with bright, detailed highs, a full, present mid-range, and solid but not overly powerful bass. It definitely has a wider sound stage than its closed-back counterparts, though it's not quite as wide or as open as some open-back headsets (such as the Audeze LCD-GX). Mid-range-heavy songs such as K-931's Lonely World and Enya's Orinoco Flow sounded especially dynamic. The headset has a built-in "HyperX Bass Tube" designed to maintain powerful bass, despite its open-back style. This works decently well — while I still found bass to be more powerful on closed-back headsets such as the Razer BlackShark V3 Pro, the bass was definitely present (and fairly detailed — I could hear the full run of the bass drum in Lorde's Royals).
Games sound even better on the Cloud Alpha Air, thanks to the open-back design. Games with multi-layered audio environments, such as Uncharted 4 and God of War: Ragnarok, really stood out on the headset — I could hear every individual creature in jungles and make out conversations with (possibly unrealistic) clarity in cities. Directional audio was also very good, though I would probably still opt for a closed-back headset for competitive first-person shooters where the direction of footsteps and gunshots is paramount. But you can't beat open-back headsets for exploring an open world (and for being able to hear things happening in the real world).
Microphone of the Cloud Alpha Air
The Cloud Alpha Air has a detachable 10mm boom microphone with a unidirectional polar pattern. It sits at the end of a 3-inch flexible metal gooseneck you can bend toward your mouth for better pickup, and the arm has a small red indicator light near the microphone end that lets you know when it's muted. It's the same microphone found on HyperX's other premium headsets, including the Cloud III S Wireless and the Cloud Alpha 2 Wireless.
The mic performs about as well as expected — it's good for a headset mic, but it's definitely still a headset mic. My voice was clear and full-sounding over both voice chat and in recordings. But the mic's pickup was pretty low by default — for other HyperX headsets I've been able to adjust the gain in its Ngenuity software, but I wasn't able to get Ngenuity to recognize the Cloud Alpha Air (I imagine if it had recognized it, it would have been adjustable, however). Hopefully this is fixed in a software or firmware update soon.
The mic mute button is easy to press, and the indicator light is a nice thought — but it was too low and too dim to be useful to me (I had to keep moving the mic up to see it, which seems like it sort of defeats the purpose of having an unobtrusive indicator light). I also had the same issue I did with the mute mic button on the HyperX Cloud III wired headset, where pressing the mute button caused a noticeable blip in my recordings.
Features and Software of the Cloud Alpha Air
The Cloud Alpha Air is supposed to be configurable with HyperX's Ngenuity peripheral software, which should let you do things such as tune the EQ and adjust the microphone's input gain. But, again, I couldn't get any version of Ngenuity to recognize the Cloud Alpha Air.
Bottom Line
If you've been thinking of getting an open-back gaming headset, the Cloud Alpha Air might be the headset you've been waiting for. As long as you don't mind the wires, it's an excellent headset for the price — it's comfortable, lightweight, and it sounds great whether you're listening to music, watching movies, or gaming. While I couldn't get it to connect to Ngenuity, I honestly don't count that as much of a point against it — peripheral software often causes more headaches than it's worth, especially for a headset that's mostly analog to begin with.
Sarah Jacobsson Purewal is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware covering peripherals, software, and custom builds. You can find more of her work in PCWorld, Macworld, TechHive, CNET, Gizmodo, Tom's Guide, PC Gamer, Men's Health, Men's Fitness, SHAPE, Cosmopolitan, and just about everywhere else.

articles.text:
India’s massive AI opportunity; Women entrepreneurs in this year’s Mann Ki Baat
Unlike previous digital revolutions (internet and smartphones) that democratised access, AI is democratising intelligence itself, raising overall productivity across sectors.
Dear Reader,
The high-stakes game for India’s satellite internet is on.
Reliance Industries has officially responded to Elon Musk’s sharp critiques of India’s satellite communications landscape. Breaking its silence, the conglomerate welcomed incoming competition, saying that a competitive market ultimately serves customers best, provided every player abides by Indian law. Setting "the facts on record," Reliance directly addressed Musk's push for open competition.
Meanwhile AI company RapidCanvas has raised $29 million in Series B funding led by Vertex Ventures SEA & India. The round also saw participation from Hitachi Ventures and existing investors, including Accel, Peak XV Partners, Valley Capital Partners and Titanium Ventures.
It plans to use the capital to grow its go-to-market teams and expand its network of private equity and advisory partners, who bring managed AI execution to their portfolio companies and clients. It will also expand its field AI engineering team across India, the US and Brazil.
ICYMI: The grand finale of TechSparks featured Professor Ashok Jhunjhunwala, Institute Professor at IIT Madras and Chairman of IIIT Hyderabad and the ITEL Foundation, Food Pharmer Revant Himatsingka and more.
Lastly, Tesla has unveiled its next-generation Roadster in Texas, showcasing SpaceX-developed thrusters that reportedly enable the electric sports car to hover and maneuver in mid-air. Presenting the vehicle at a SpaceX facility, CEO Elon Musk teased the crowd with a preview of its wild capabilities: “You're going to see some crazy stuff tonight.”
However, it is unlikely that we will see flying cars anytime soon. Here’s why.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- India’s massive AI opportunity
- Women entrepreneurs in this year’s Mann Ki Baat
Here’s your trivia for today: What consumer tech brand takes its name from the Swedish words for "electric" and "light" after a landmark merger in 1919? (Scroll down for the answer)
TechSparks
India’s massive AI opportunity
At TechSparks 2026, industry leaders Ashutosh Sharma from Prosus and Keshav Reddy from Equal AI discussed India’s rapidly growing AI landscape during a session hosted by Shradha Sharma. They emphasised that while current discussions focus on a $100 billion opportunity, AI could eventually add up to $1 trillion to India's GDP by 2035.
Unlike previous digital revolutions (internet and smartphones) that democratised access, AI is democratising intelligence itself, raising overall productivity across sectors.
Key takeaways:
- To capitalise on this shift, Indian startups must leverage local nuances to solve large, unaddressed domestic problems in areas like healthcare, education, and consumer services (such as spam call management).
- Ashutosh Sharma, Head of Investments and M&A, India, Prosus, said local understanding would be a key differentiator for Indian startups competing with international companies.
- Success lies in targeting specific, widespread local pain points. As an example, Reddy spoke about Equal AI scaling to millions of users by addressing India's severe spam call issue.
Inspiration
Women entrepreneurs in this year’s Mann Ki Baat
Across India, women are transforming local skills and natural resources into thriving ventures—spanning floriculture, solar energy, and sustainable fish farming.
Featured on Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Mann Ki Baat in 2026, their success stories underscore a powerful playbook for rural economic growth: combining hands-on training and institutional backing with reliable credit and direct market connections allows women entrepreneurs to build sustainable businesses.
Key takeaways:
- Sujata Bhuyan, a homemaker from Odisha’s Sambalpur district, ventured into fish farming to supplement her family’s income. Her annual fish production has increased to 25-30 metric tonnes, earning her an annual income of Rs 7–10 lakh, according to the Indian Council of Agricultural Research
- Payal Munjpara, from Surendranagar district in Gujarat, has become a solar entrepreneur. As a solar technician, Munjpara works on rooftop solar installations across neighbouring districts, earning a livelihood through her skills.
- Babita Sharma, a street vendor from Nandgram in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, turned a small roadside stall selling religious offerings into a growing business with support from the PM Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme.
News & updates
- Onboarding: Real estate classifieds Magicbricks has appointed Mayank Jain as chief executive officer (CEO), effective October 1. In a statement on Friday, Magicbricks, one of the leading property platforms, said Jain has joined from CarDekho, where he served for over five years as CEO of Auto Classifieds.
- In the red: Maestroedge Solutions, which runs home services platform Snabbit, has posted a net loss of Rs 167.75 crore for 2025-26, nearly 30 times lower than the previous year, as spending on service providers, marketing and staff rose with the expansion of its business.
What consumer tech brand takes its name from the Swedish words for "electric" and "light" after a landmark merger in 1919?
Answer: Electrolux

articles.title: Ce vélo vendu par une marque inattendue change de vitesse tout seul
articles.text:
Honor se met en selle avec un vélo électrique pliant à deux vitesses automatiques
Du smartphone au guidon
Honor ajoute un vélo électrique pliant à son catalogue. Cet Ado Air 20 Pro associe deux vitesses automatiques, une courroie et une batterie amovible.
Honor surprend avec un nouvel arrivant que l'on n'attendait pas dans son rayon Sport & Santé avec le HONOR Choice Ado Air 20 Pro. Ce vélo à roues de 20 pouces embarque un moteur arrière de 250 W et une transmission interne à deux rapports. Le changement s’effectue automatiquement selon l’allure. Le petit rapport facilite les démarrages tandis que le second évite de mouliner lorsque la vitesse augmente. Des capteurs de couple ajustent l’assistance à l’effort exercé sur les pédales.
La chaîne prend congé
Une courroie en fibre de carbone remplace la chaîne, ce qui dispense d'un peu d'entretien. Le vélo reçoit aussi une fourche suspendue verrouillable et des freins à disque hydrauliques de 160 mm. Garde-boue, porte-bagages, feu arrière et clignotants sont aussi de la partie.
Logée dans la tige de selle, la batterie amovible de 370 Wh peut se recharger séparément. Honor annonce jusqu’à 100 km d’autonomie. Cette valeur dépend évidemment du relief, de l’assistance utilisée et du poids du cycliste. Une carte NFC permet le déverrouillage, tandis que l’application Ado EBIKE donne accès aux réglages et aux données de trajet.
Plié, pas poids plume
Le pliage prendrait une dizaine de secondes. Le vélo mesure alors 90 × 43 × 67 cm, pour environ 21 kg. Une donnée à prendre en compte avant d’Adopter un trajet avec correspondance par les escaliers.
Annoncé disponible depuis le 8 octobre en gris à 1699,90 €, il bénéficie d’une offre jusqu’au 8 novembre. Une remise de 100 € associée à 100 € de coupon ramènent le tarif à 1499,90 €.

articles.title: Un puñado de rocas de Sudáfrica tiene en sus manos resolver el gran misterio del oxígeno en la Tierra
articles.text:
Hace unos 2.400 millones de años, tuvo lugar la Gran Oxidación, un proceso en el cual el oxígeno se acumuló en la atmósfera en una cantidad suficiente para promover la aparición de formas de vida complejas. Sin embargo, en nuestro planeta había muchos procesos que funcionaban como sumideros para este oxígeno: gases volcánicos, descomposición de la materia orgánica, minerales que se oxidan…
La aparición de oxígeno podría haber sido un visto y no visto, pero no fue así. Ocurrió algo que hizo que ese gas se mantuviese, permitiendo que la vida compleja avanzase más y más hasta llegar a nuestros días. El mecanismo que favoreció todo esto ha sido un misterio durante mucho tiempo, pero ahora podríamos tener la respuesta que buscábamos, gracias al estudio publicado a partir del análisis de unas rocas en Sudáfrica.
El reciclaje que hizo proliferar la vida. Tras la Gran Oxidación, muchos de los sulfuros que se encontraban en los continentes se combinaron con oxígeno, para dar lugar a otras moléculas conocidas como sulfatos. Estos, a su vez, fueron arrastrados hasta el mar, donde pusieron a trabajar a las bacterias sulfatorreductoras, unos microorganismos que descomponen la materia orgánica, extrayéndole electrones que luego van a parar a los sulfatos. Sin esos sulfatos, no pueden trabajar adecuadamente. Por eso, proliferaron muchísimo, descomponiendo una gran cantidad de la materia orgánica que se depositaba en el mar. Dicha descomposición liberó mucho fósforo, un nutriente que permitió que proliferasen aún más seres vivos en los océanos.
Si hay más seres vivos, hay más materia orgánica que se acumula en el fondo marino cuando estos mueren. Llegó a haber tanta que las bacterias sulfatorreductoras no daban abasto. Parte de esa materia orgánica acababa sepultada, de modo que el carbono que la compone se enterraba con ella. Ese carbono enterrado, por lo tanto, dejó de oxidarse, favoreciendo que el oxígeno de la fotosíntesis no se consumiera y permaneciese en la atmósfera. Con todo esto, más oxígeno permitía oxidar más sulfuros continentales y el ciclo se retroalimentaba.
Las rocas que tenían las respuestas. Todo esto es una hipótesis lanzada por un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de California en Riverside después de analizar una serie de rocas recogidas en Sudáfrica. Recurrieron a una técnica que permite disolver los componentes minerales de las rocas de uno en uno, de manera que no se mide el fósforo total, sino que se puede medir de qué mineral viene cada fracción de fósforo.
Así, vieron que una parte estaba unida a materia orgánica o a óxidos de hierro, o formó minerales en el propio fondo marino. Ese fósforo, por lo tanto, estuvo ligado al ciclo biológico y su cantidad refleja cuánto se reciclaba. Por otro lado, había fósforo presente en granos minerales arrastrados desde el continente. Este nunca estuvo disponible para los organismos, por lo que no tiene nada que ver con la proliferación de vida en la Tierra primitiva. El primero era muy abundante, por lo que todo apunta a ese reciclaje que hemos visto paso a paso.
Aun así, la vida compleja tardó en aparecer. Tradicionalmente se ha pensado que la vida compleja tardó en aparecer porque no habría suficiente oxígeno disponible. Sin embargo, esta hipótesis apunta a que había de sobra. Por eso, para que esta pueda sostenerse, los autores del estudio sugieren que este hecho pudo deberse a otras causas ambientales o biológicas. Por ejemplo, una glaciación o problemas de disponibilidad de otros nutrientes.
Aplicaciones en el presente. Todo este hallazgo no sirve solo para comprender cómo surgió la vida en la Tierra. También puede tener aplicaciones en el presente. Por un lado, el cambio climático está limitando el oxígeno en los océanos en algunas regiones de nuestro planeta, por lo que si entendemos lo que ocurrió en el pasado podemos anticiparnos al futuro y evitar males mayores. Por otro lado, toda esta información puede ser útil para seleccionar planetas susceptibles de albergar vida más allá de la Tierra. En definitiva, estas rocas de Sudáfrica nos han dado información útil para entender el pasado, proteger el presente y afrontar el futuro.

articles.title: Moins de 650€ pour un PC 14 pouces avec 16 Go de RAM : le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 est en promo ce weekend.
articles.text:
Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 de 14 pouces, dans sa version Core 5 210H avec 16 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de stockage, s’affiche à 649,99 € chez Amazon au lieu de 779,99 €. Une configuration de PC bureautique bien dosée, dont l’écran reste le point faible.
Lenovo décline son IdeaPad Slim 3 en 14 pouces avec une puce Intel Core 5 210H, 16 Go de mémoire vive et un SSD de 512 Go, le tout sous Windows 11 Home. C’est une configuration pensée pour la bureautique, les études et le multimédia, dans un châssis de 1,39 kg.
Amazon, qui le vend en exclusivité, affiche une offre à durée limitée qui fait passer l’IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces à 649,99 € au lieu d’un prix conseillé de 779,99 €, soit 130 € d’économie. Reste à savoir à qui cette machine convient vraiment, car son écran ne suit pas tout à fait le reste de la fiche technique.
Le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 pouces (Core 5 210H, 16 Go, 512 Go) est proposé à 649,99 € au lieu de 779,99 € chez Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14 ?
- Un processeur H et 16 Go de mémoire : Le Core 5 210H aligne 8 cœurs et 12 threads jusqu’à 4,8 GHz, épaulés par 16 Go de DDR5. C’est le socle que nous recommandons pour un PC bureautique appelé à durer.
- Un stockage extensible : Le SSD de 512 Go en PCIe 4.0 occupe l’un des deux emplacements M.2 2242, et le second reste libre pour accueillir un autre SSD. Une évolution simple le jour où photos et documents finissent par saturer le disque.
- Un écran 16:10 et une connectique complète : La dalle WUXGA de 1 920 x 1 200 pixels affiche plus de lignes qu’un écran 16:9, utile sur un tableur. Deux USB-A, un USB-C, un HDMI et un lecteur SD évitent la plupart des adaptateurs.
Pour les cours, le télétravail et un poste fixe au bureau
Cet IdeaPad Slim 3 se destine à la bureautique, à la navigation et à la vidéo. Son port USB-C gère la recharge et la sortie DisplayPort, et la machine pilote deux écrans externes en plus du sien : reliée à un moniteur, elle devient un poste de travail complet. Le cache de webcam et le double micro servent les visioconférences, et Lenovo annonce environ deux heures d’autonomie pour 15 minutes de charge rapide.
Il conviendra à un étudiant, à un télétravailleur ou à un foyer qui veut un ordinateur familial sous 650 €. Il convient moins aux créatifs : la dalle IPS plafonne à 300 nits et couvre 45 % du gamut NTSC, trop peu pour retoucher des photos avec des couleurs fidèles. Le jeu se limite aux titres légers, la partie graphique intégrée Intel UHD restant modeste. Enfin, 8 Go de mémoire sont soudés à la carte mère et la capacité totale plafonne à 24 Go.
Ce qu’il vaut face aux autres PC bureautiques
Ce modèle coche la plupart des critères que nous retenons pour un PC bureautique : définition WUXGA, Core 5 et 16 Go de mémoire. Il fait l’impasse sur un écran au-delà de 60 Hz et sur une colorimétrie étendue, et sa puce Raptor Lake, sans NPU, n’ouvre pas les fonctions Copilot+ de Windows. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs PC portables pour la bureautique, le modèle le moins cher, l’Acer Swift Air 14, offre un écran 120 Hz mais s’affiche autour de 800 € au moment où nous écrivons. L’IdeaPad joue la carte du prix, au détriment du confort visuel.
✅ Les points forts
- Core 5 210H à 8 cœurs et 16 Go de DDR5
- Second emplacement M.2 libre pour ajouter un SSD
- Écran 16:10 WUXGA antireflet
- Connectique variée, avec lecteur SD et recharge en USB-C
- 1,39 kg pour un 14 pouces
❌ Les limites
- Écran limité à 45 % NTSC, 300 nits et 60 Hz
- 8 Go soudés, 24 Go au maximum
- Pas de NPU, donc pas de fonctions Copilot+
- Pas de lecteur d’empreintes, HDMI 1.4 limité à la 4K en 30 Hz
Amazon présente cette baisse à 649,99 € comme une offre à durée limitée, sans en préciser la fin : le prix affiché sur la fiche produit fait foi.
À 649,99 €, cet IdeaPad Slim 3 offre une base saine pour travailler : 8 cœurs, 16 Go de mémoire, un SSD rapide et la place pour un second. Le format 16:10 et la connectique complète en font un outil pratique, au bureau comme en déplacement. Les 130 € de remise se calculent sur un prix conseillé, une référence de catalogue plutôt qu’un historique de prix.
L’écran reste le compromis à accepter : suffisant sur le papier pour le texte et la vidéo, il ne convient ni à la retouche photo ni à qui attend la fluidité d’une dalle 120 Hz. Étudiants, télétravailleurs et familles y trouveront un ordinateur équilibré pour leur budget. Ceux qui travaillent l’image ont intérêt à viser plus haut, mais pour un usage bureautique au long cours, sa capacité d’évolution pèse réellement.

articles.title: 10 of the coolest retro gadgets we've spotted this year — from film cameras to home phones and cassette players
articles.text:
Retro tech is making a comeback — here are 10 of the raddest old skool gadgets we've spotted, from cassette players to flip phones and film cameras
A nostalgic antidote to subscription overload and unwanted AI
Retro tech is having a real moment right now. As modern gadgets get ever flashier and more powerful, it seems the zeitgeist is pulling the other way, with a wave of clunky, analogue, nostalgic tech. Since the start of the year, we've spotted retro gadgets popping up in every corner of the tech world. I've rounded up some of my favorites below — hit the View details button to learn more about each one.
Some of these gadgets offer modern functionality behind an old-school casing. The viral Casio F-B100W is a clunky digital watch that can track your step count. The Sudo is an in-development, iPod-alike music player — complete with audio jack and click wheel for maximum satisfaction — but it will let you access music streaming services.
For others, the simplicity is entirely the point. The Pinwheel Home phone is a wall phone that can only call approved contacts, enabling tweens to chat to their friends without the specter of social media lingering in the air. And while the Nokia 300 Charge is 'modern' in that it's not attached to a wall with a curly cable, the flashiest thing about it might be its flashlight (4x brighter than you'll find on a Nokia 105, don't you know).
You'll actually own the music you play on the Miko portable cassette player, and although there's no accounting for audio quality, at least you know you won't encounter any AI slop-bops. Meanwhile, if you've got a phone that's crammed with snaps you never look at, perhaps reverting to film with a Kodak Snapic A1 will be enough to get you engaging with your photos again.
