articles.title: Apple cambia las reglas de App Store contra apps que generan imágenes íntimas con IA
articles.text:
Apple actualizó las reglas de la tienda App Store para prohibir de manera más explícita las aplicaciones que usan inteligencia artificial para generar imágenes íntimas sin el consentimiento de las personas retratadas. El cambio llega después de una serie de escándalos ligados a Grok, el chatbot de xAI.
La sección 1.2 de las Pautas de Revisión de Apps, que regula el contenido generado por usuarios, ahora advierte de forma directa sobre “infracciones de propiedad intelectual, imágenes íntimas no consentidas y acoso anónimo”.
El texto agrega que los desarrolladores que no implementen resguardos adecuados, o no corrijan violaciones ya notificadas, pueden considerarse en infracción del Código de Conducta para Desarrolladores.
Apple crea nueva sección en App Store
Apple también creó una sección nueva, la 2.5.19, dirigida contra las apps de “cebo y cambio”: programas que se presentan como herramientas inofensivas durante la revisión y después, ya aprobados, activan funciones dañinas como la generación de imágenes indebidad falsas.
La norma prohíbe ocultar funciones mediante ofuscación de código y advierte que esa práctica puede derivar en la eliminación de la app y el cierre de la cuenta del desarrollador.
La compañía, además, endureció el lenguaje de la sección legal de sus pautas: las apps que faciliten trata de personas o explotación infantil “serán eliminadas de la App Store y bloqueadas de la distribución alternativa”.
El antecedente de Grok ante la problemática de imágenes falsas
La decisión llega después de que usuarios de X utilizaran Grok a comienzos de este año para crear escenas íntimas falsas no consentidos de mujeres, incluidas menores. Apple no retiró X ni Grok de la App Store en ese momento, aunque le dijo a senadores estadounidenses que había amenazado con hacerlo si xAI no corregía el problema.
En junio, durante la conferencia de desarrolladores WWDC, manifestantes pidieron frente a las oficinas de Apple que la compañía eliminara a Grok, a X y toda la tecnología relacionada de su tienda de aplicaciones.
En julio pasado, el fiscal de la ciudad de San Francisco, David Chiu, había ordenado a Apple retirar trece aplicaciones capaces de generar imágenes sexuales no consentidas, algo que la empresa dijo haber cumplido.
Según TechCrunch, Chiu acusó a Apple y a Google de “ayudar y encubrir” la venta de pornografía ultrafalsa ilegal y de haber ganado millones de dólares en comisiones por esas apps.
Chiu había dicho entonces que generar imágenes íntimas no consentidas es “ilegal, dañino y completamente inaceptable”, y advirtió que su oficina seguiría presionando a ambas empresas si no reforzaban los controles de sus tiendas.
Una investigación del Tech Transparency Project, un grupo de vigilancia independiente, había identificado en enero de 2026, decenas de aplicaciones de este tipo disponibles en la App Store. En abril del mismo año, el mismo grupo reveló que las sugerencias de búsqueda y los anuncios de la propia tienda también dirigían a los usuarios hacia esas apps.
Según datos compilados por una firma de análisis móvil y citados por TechSpot, las aplicaciones identificadas por el Tech Transparency Project acumularon 483 millones de descargas y generaron más de 122 millones de dólares en ingresos combinados entre la App Store y Google Play.
Un estudio de las universidades de Cornell y Georgetown había identificado 420 aplicaciones de intercambio de rostros en ambas tiendas.
Los investigadores probaron 155 de ellas y encontraron que el 70% permitía colocar el rostro de una persona sobre una imagen desnuda sin ninguna salvaguarda técnica. Ninguna de esas apps se anunciaba como una herramienta de ese tipo, según el estudio.
Las obligaciones para los desarrolladores en App Store
Con las nuevas reglas, los desarrolladores “deben prevenir y eliminar de manera proactiva” las imágenes sexuales no consentidas como parte de los requisitos de moderación de contenido para las apps de la tienda. Quienes no implementen resguardos suficientes o no corrijan violaciones tras ser notificados pueden ser retirados de la App Store.
Apple también aclaró su regla contra las apps de “cebo y cambio”, que agregan o modifican funciones, incluida la generación de imágenes falsas, después de haber sido aprobadas en la revisión inicial. Esa conducta ya estaba prohibida en una sección distinta de las pautas, pero la compañía decidió nombrarla de manera explícita.
Apple ya había defendido su política frente a estos casos. “App Store fue diseñada para ser un lugar seguro y confiable, y siempre prohibimos estrictamente las apps diseñadas para generar, distribuir o consumir pornografía”.

articles.title: 10 Milliarden Jahre altes Radiosignal erreicht die Erde – Teleskope finden den Ursprung
articles.text:
Älter als unsere Sonne: Wie ein 10 Milliarden Jahre altes Radiosignal die Erde erreichte
Ein internationales Forschungsteam hat das bislang am weitesten entfernte Radiosignal der Astronomiegeschichte aufgezeichnet. Der als Fast Radio Burst bekannte Ausbruch reiste mehr als zehn Milliarden Jahre durch das Weltall, bevor er die Erde erreichte und von den Instrumenten der Wissenschaftler:innen verarbeitet werden konnte.
Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entstand das Signal mit der Bezeichnung FRB 20240304B, als das Universum erst etwa drei Milliarden Jahre alt war. Die initiale Aufzeichnung gelang zunächst mit dem Radioteleskop MeerKAT in der südafrikanischen Provinz Nordkap, das für derartige Himmelsdurchmusterungen konstruiert wurde.
James-Webb-Teleskop lokalisiert den Ursprung
Um den Ursprungsort zu bestimmen, nutzten die Astronom:innen im Nachgang das James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa. Dessen Infrarotinstrumente zeigten bei der Analyse, dass der Ausbruch aus einer sehr kleinen Galaxie stammt, die aktuell in hoher Geschwindigkeit neue Sterne bildet.
Diese Galaxie weist im direkten Vergleich zu unserer Milchstraße nur einen geringen Anteil an schweren Elementen auf. Der Astronom Themiya Nanayakkara von der Universität Sydney im australischen Bundesstaat New South Wales erklärte gegenüber The Guardian, dass zum Zeitpunkt der Signalentstehung weder die Erde noch die Sonne existierten.
Magnetare als wahrscheinliche Quelle der Ausbrüche
Fast Radio Bursts sind kurze Radiowellen-Ausbrüche, die in wenigen Millisekunden so viel Energie freisetzen wie unsere Sonne in mehreren Monaten oder Jahren. Seit ihrer ersten Entdeckung im Jahr 2007, als der US-Astrophysiker Duncan Lorimer einen solchen Ausbruch in alten Archivdaten der Magellanschen Wolken fand, wird in der Astronomie über die physikalische Ursache diskutiert.
Die Signale lassen sich identifizieren, weil sie auf ihrem Weg durch den intergalaktischen Raum verschiedene Frequenzen unterschiedlich schnell transportieren. Niedrigere Radiofrequenzen werden durch ionisiertes Plasma im Weltraum stärker gebremst als hohe Frequenzen, wodurch das Signal verzerrt auf der Erde eintrifft und sich die zurückgelegte Distanz berechnen lässt.
Eine in der Forschungsgemeinschaft gängige Theorie besagt, dass sogenannte Magnetare für diese Radioausbrüche verantwortlich sind. Dabei handelt es sich um dichte Neutronensterne mit einem starken Magnetfeld, die in der Regel als Überrest einer Supernova-Explosion entstehen.
Kosmische Materie mit Radiosignalen berechnen
Für die wissenschaftliche Analyse sind diese Signale auch unabhängig von ihrer Entstehung wertvoll, da Fast Radio Bursts durch die mikroskopischen Partikel beeinflusst werden, die sie auf ihrem Weg durch das All durchqueren. Der Astrophysiker Matthew Bailes von der Swinburne Universität im australischen Bundesstaat Victoria beschreibt die Signale daher als mechanische Methode, um die Atome im Universum auf großen Distanzen zu zählen.
Laut der Astrophysikerin Sara Webb, die ebenfalls an der Swinburne Universität tätig ist, funktionieren die Ausbrüche wie eine Sichtlinien-Zählung für die Materie, die sie auf dem Weg zur Erde passieren müssen. Seit der ersten Entdeckung im Jahr 2007 wurden mehr als 10.000 Fast Radio Bursts registriert, wobei sich einige kontinuierlich wiederholen und andere lediglich als einmaliges Ereignis auftreten.
Ob der nun lokalisierte Ausbruch FRB 20240304B in der näheren Zukunft weitere Signale in Richtung unseres Sonnensystems senden wird, müssen nachfolgende astronomische Beobachtungen zeigen. Bis dahin werten die Astronom:innen die bisherigen und gespeicherten Datenströme systematisch aus, um Rückschlüsse auf die Verteilung der Materie im frühen Universum zu ziehen.

articles.title: Rep. Ritchie Torres Wants Gamers to Own the Games They Buy, Announces Power To The Players Act
articles.text:
Saturday, October 17th 2026
Rep. Ritchie Torres Wants Gamers to Own the Games They Buy, Announces Power To The Players Act
U.S. Representative Ritchie Torres (D-NY) has announced plans to introduce the "Power To The Players Act," a federal bill that would direct the FTC to write rules making a game purchase actual ownership rather than a revocable license. Games that rely on online servers would also need to offer an offline mode before those servers are switched off, and players would keep the right to transfer the games they buy. The bill hasn't been formally introduced yet, so there's no bill text, and Torres hasn't confirmed any cosponsors. Torres pointed to NBA 2K25 as the example. The game sold for $69.99, or $99.99 for the All-Star Edition, and it leaves digital storefronts on October 30, with online servers shutting down at the end of the year, roughly two years after launch. Here's how Torres put it:
When you pay for a game, you should own it. Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale. Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.
The push follows the Stop Killing Games campaign, which gathered nearly 1.3 million verified signatures in the EU, only for the European Commission to decline a legal obligation in June and offer talks on a voluntary industry code instead. California's Protect Our Games Act also stalled in a state Senate committee, with the ESA opposing it. A federal bill faces an even longer road, and the transfer right in particular would effectively mean digital resale that no major storefront allows today, so heavy industry pushback seems likely.
Sources:
				Rep. Ritchie Torres, 				via Kotaku

articles.title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year, according to a report that the AI company published on Friday.
Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates.
Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%.
Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.”
One employee reportedly described an “eternal pressure at Anthropic to move as fast as possible and use Claude for everything.” In an April 2026 survey, 27% of employees said they had become more productive because of Claude and 20% said their job had shifted “from actually doing work to managing Claudes”; apparently one engineered compared this to babysitting: “When you are babysitting, every child brings to you concerns with an equal demand for your attention and the various [Claudes] also do that.”
In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized.
Unsurprisingly, the report argues that AI adoption has made the company more productive, as indicated by “more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.” The company acknowledges that “more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact,” but it also hasn’t found any indications that code quality is declining.
The report says that based on calendar data, meeting time per employee is up 20% compared to a year ago, and it’s up 16% for technical contributors. The company attributes this to the importance of “human trust and accountability,” with employees repeatedly describing “face-to-face coordination as indispensable.”

articles.title: Why BioWare's Neverwinter Nights still has thousands of active players
articles.text:
Neverwinter Nights was made by the studio that produced seminal RPGs Baldur’s Gate, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age. It sold well and was critically acclaimed at launch. Yet, somehow, it has not been canonized in most gamers’ minds over the decades the same way the games that came before and after it were.
Nonetheless, more than two decades later, it still has a tight-knit and surprisingly active community that none of those other games can rival. I think that’s partly because it was a completely different beast.
BioWare is known for making multi-character, story-driven role-playing games that focused primarily on single-player story campaigns, though some supported co-op play in those campaigns. With Neverwinter Nights, BioWare instead made a game that was as focused on a modding toolset for content creation as it was on giving players a pre-packaged story, and that emphasized multiplayer at least as much as solo play.
Today you would expect this to be a calculated attempt to bring more long-term, always-on, multiplayer-as-a-service to an RPG franchise that has mostly appealed to solo players. You might imagine it would be about selling cosmetics, a subscription, or a battle pass, or maybe you would think it was about nabbing appealing engagement numbers.
But it’s clear from playing it today that Neverwinter Nights wasn’t primarily made for those reasons. Instead, it came from a passion for tabletop role-playing and a desire to get closer to that in video game form than ever before.
Yes, the BioWare team noted in some interviews that they saw this as a trial run for exploring the idea of making a massively multiplayer game (MMO)—something that, in the year 2000, was seen by many as the hot new business opportunity in gaming, and which was in many ways the precursor to the games-as-a-service we see today. They then indicated they realized that an MMO was harder to make than they had assumed and abandoned that ambition well before Neverwinter Nights shipped.
Neverwinter Nights is not exactly an MMO. Instead, it’s designed for small communities of people to inhabit and create with, and it features a powerful toolset for virtual dungeon masters to use to subject regular players to challenges in an improvisational way on a live server.
“We always envisioned it as a table with four legs—the single player, the multiplayer, the DMing tools and the toolset (the module making tools),” BioWare’s Ray Muzyka told IGN around the time the game was released. “They all appeal to different groups, and we’ve tried to make them all equivalently high quality.”
Over the past month, I’ve been replaying Neverwinter Nights‘ main story campaign, The Wailing Death, as a solo player, for the first time in 20 years. The nostalgia has been strong in this replay, but I have also found that BioWare didn’t quite nail “equivalently high quality” for all the pillars. Still, it doesn’t matter, because as we’ll see when we check in with the game’s community, the campaign is not the point.
“The single player experience has to be as good as anything we’ve ever done in [Baldur’s Gate], [Baldur’s Gate 2], or Throne of Bhaal and hopefully better,” Muzyka told IGN. “Our goal here at BioWare is that each game we do has to be better than the previous one.”
If single-player is one of the legs, it might be fair to call Neverwinter Nights‘ table a little wobbly. It still stands, but you know how irritating it can be.
For example, Neverwinter Nights leaves behind Baldur’s Gate or Icewind Dale‘s party-based systems, and instead has the player controlling just one character directly. It makes sense for a multiplayer game, but doesn’t work as well for a single-player experience in this case—at least with the Dungeons & Dragons rules of the time.
I chose to play a monk, a martial arts specialist, simply because I’ve always been drawn to that particular fantasy identity, and because I’d never played one in a D&D game. I regretted that decision after a while.
For many of the character levels covered in The Wailing Death, the monk basically just picks between two fighting modes: one that misses more but attacks more frequently, and one that’s just normal. That, along with some intense restrictions on which weapons or armor can be used while keeping all their benefits, and a couple of knockdown and stun attacks that often don’t work, make up the whole kit for many hours of playtime, particularly in the first act. (It does get better later on, though.)
The original campaign is fun and nostalgic, but it’s arguably not BioWare’s best.
The original campaign is fun and nostalgic, but it’s arguably not BioWare’s best.
Credit:
GOG
A kit like this makes sense in a pen-and-paper RPG with a live dungeon master (DM), because the player and DM can work together to invent creative expressions of their abilities, and it works in a party in a video game because it’s just one of multiple complementary characters with a wide range of skills and spells.
But for a game that is about 80 percent battling enemies without controlling any other characters, it gets monotonous quickly. There aren’t as many meaningful character builds, gearing, or tactical choices as you’re used to in some other RPGs until quite a ways into the campaign. Often, you just run in and watch the dice roll until either you die or the enemy dies, while sometimes drinking potions.
This problem is less severe with some other classes, but the tension is usually there to some degree.
Whereas Baldur’s Gate 2, for example, had a partial authored background for your character that then played into the narrative, Neverwinter Nights leaves you as an Elder Scrolls-like blank slate. I normally love that! It’s good for role-playing with friends, because you can make up your own character completely. But it means the story can’t be character-driven, and the gameplay doesn’t provide enough flexibility or freedom in return.
Still, I enjoyed my experience with the campaign when I replayed it recently, even if it couldn’t match Baldur’s Gate 2, Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, or other BioWare classics for me personally. While the story wasn’t anything special by BioWare’s standards, there was something genuinely cozy to me about the genericness of the narrative. It took me back to an earlier time in CRPGs, before things got quite so precious. “This is just like D&D!” was still enough to sell it on its own. Maybe it’s just nostalgia, though.
Since most people played the game solo, and it was a relatively small portion of the player base that dove deep into the construction kit or DM tools, I think this is the main reason Neverwinter Nights has not achieved the same pantheon status as other BioWare titles that came before and after it.
But for those lucky few who were invested in those other table legs, it actually was quite special—and amazingly, it remains so today.
The persistent worlds of Neverwinter Nights
“The main thing I would shout from the rooftops if I could, is that firing up Neverwinter Nights and launching its original campaign… does not do justice to what Neverwinter Nights has become since,” a longtime player named Daniel Morris told me. He goes by Irongron in the community, and he runs Arelith, which is both one of the OG persistent multiplayer servers and one of the most popular servers today. Morris is also working on a visual overhaul of the original campaign; he hopes to release it next year.
Arelith hit its peak player count “a little less than two years ago,” as Morris tells it—not way back when the game was new. “Our community is the heart of Arelith, it’s not just our audience, but where we find our DMs and developers,” he said.
Arelith is a fountain of creativity; for example, this is original artwork commissioned for the game’s loading screens from artist Matheus Graef.
Arelith is a fountain of creativity; for example, this is original artwork commissioned for the game’s loading screens from artist Matheus Graef.
Credit:
Matheus Graef
I spent many evenings in my younger days playing multi-user dungeons (MUDs), the text-based online role-playing games that preceded MMOs like EverQuest or World of Warcraft. While there were big MUDs, many were small communities of just one or two dozen people, and often, those same people were the ones actually making the game’s content. For example, I was a room builder for one MUD; I wrote the descriptions for places in the MUD’s world and decided which monsters, NPCs, or items inhabited those places.
Neverwinter Nights‘ multiplayer platform and community—both as it was back in the 2000s and as it is today—reminds me of those MUD days. There’s an ownership of that shared world that is entirely lost in the MMO days, perhaps more akin to a modern, small Minecraft server than an MMO with thousands of users.
That seems to be part of the appeal for a player I spoke with who goes by the name NelaK in the community, and who has, among other things, taken over maintenance and moderation of the Neverwinter Vault, the community’s de facto hub for two decades. The website hosts news, patches, assets, mods, a forum, a wiki, and an associated Discord server.
“It’s not an MMO, and that’s a good thing in my opinion. The communities are smaller, which means your roleplay and your actions matter and can affect the world,” said NelaK. “The world itself can be tailored around what the players want. That’s a unique thing that you can’t get from an MMO or from smaller-scale multiplayer games. It sits in a sweet spot where you can have enough players that it feels like a proper community and a world you can engage with while you can still matter.”
Baldur’s Gate and Icewind Dale did have multiplayer, where each player could control one or more characters directly. As noted, Neverwinter Nights limits each player to one character, but it adds a new role: a dungeon master, who can spawn enemies, occupy and act as NPCs, and more, to aid in group storytelling, similar to a pen-and-paper game.
“While Arelith is essentially a mini MMO, many of the other servers pride themselves in running highly curated, beautifully crafted campaign worlds much closer to tabletop role-playing game emulator that Neverwinter Nights was first intended as,” Morris told me. He called Neverwinter Nights “a direct translation of the tabletop role-playing game experience into the digital sphere.”
It’s as much a construction kit as it is a game
The game’s modding kit and easy-to-use scripting tools let players build scenarios relatively quickly. It essentially let players build a little RPG world, run it, and inhabit it. It was a bustling scene back then, and there’s still a community doing this today. The combination of the relative simplicity of the graphics and the elegance of the tools make this toolset an unusually excellent balance between flexible, powerful, and easy to learn.
“The tile-based areas are basic and limiting in some respects, but they do mean that building areas is quick and easy,” explained NelaK. “It’s much more approachable than a lot of other platforms.”
For NelaK and some other members of the game’s community today, the game’s tools aren’t just the remaining appeal—they’re the main appeal.
“I’ve been playing Neverwinter Nights since launch day. I remember one of my friends dragging me along to the store because they really wanted the game and I went just to keep them company,” he remembered. “I ended up buying it, and I’ve been hooked ever since, but to this day, I’ve still never played through the original campaigns… and yet I’ve played Neverwinter Nights or spent time building or working on something Neverwinter Nights-related most days since.”
I toyed around with the tools quite a bit back in the day. I remember re-creating a big chunk of the world of my favorite MMO at the time, Meridian 59, with the intent to make a story-driven, single-player campaign for that game; Meridian 59 had very little narrative as it was.
I also remember that Neverwinter Nights was for many years a common way for would-be narrative designers to make a portfolio piece for applying for jobs within the games industry. When I was in college, a close friend of mine (Brian “Psychochild” Green, who at the time co-ran Meridian 59, and sadly has since passed) offered to show my Neverwinter Nights modules to some friends of his at BioWare if I wanted to interview for a job there to write for their next game, which, based on timing, probably would have been Mass Effect. I declined in order to focus on other priorities I had at the time, for better or worse.
Similarly, many (though certainly not all) people in the community have professional backgrounds closely related to, or at least adjacent to, game development.
“Neverwinter Nights provides a unique intersection of where I can apply my technical and professional skills along with my interest in video games and do it for something that doesn’t feel like work,” said NelaK. Morris specifically noted that several members of the Arileth team work or have worked in the games industry or software development.
This is the game’s legacy, not the story campaigns that shipped with the game. And that explains the game’s relative obscurity today: that’s a more niche appeal than a really good, story-driven, single-player RPG. But for the people who are into it, there’s nothing else that quite compares.
Returning to Neverwinter Nights today
I don’t imagine most people still regularly see references to Neverwinter Nights, but I sometimes do. For the past couple of years, I’ve enjoyed the dark fantasy trend on TikTok. These are short, vertical videos set to a particular kind of 1980s fantasy-type medieval synth music, depicting imagery from what feels like a long-lost, strangely nostalgic subgenre of fantasy media that is more implied in our memories’ liminal space between real fantasy movies and books of the ’80s and early ’90s than it is something that actually specifically existed.
It turns out Neverwinter Nights‘ assets fit that milieu quite well, so I sometimes saw videos of people creating online Neverwinter Nights servers meant to capture that vibe. It’s niche as hell, but it’s there. The TikTok videos from one of the game’s servers were actually how I got inspired to try the game again.
“Over the last year there’s been a bit of a resurgence, with new servers going live, and others going viral,” Morris told me. Some player-run servers “have had hundreds of thousands interacting with their TikTok videos.”
He added that his own community’s Discord server has 5,000 members, and that’s just one part of the game’s wider audience.
If you want to get back into the game or try it for the first time, you can buy the Enhanced Edition on GOG and other storefronts; a front-page poll on the Neverwinter Vault indicates that about 65 percent of the community primarily uses that version, as compared to previous releases or the sequel, Neverwinter Nights 2.
If you want to try the single-player, the Enhanced Edition comes with a plethora of officially sanctioned campaigns of varying quality—not just The Wailing Death.
But let’s say you, like some members of the game’s current community, are more interested in multiplayer than single-player. A good place to start is the Neverwinter Vault. Additionally, Enhanced Edition developer Beamdog hosts a list of active community servers you can join.
As I write this, a few hundred people are playing across a couple dozen servers, which is impressive. I love to see old games like this keep the community going. It’s especially important for Neverwinter Nights, because more than any other BioWare game or even most other RPGs in general, this game is its community.

articles.title: Quad 8-pin mod protects the $8,500 RTX 5090 you can’t replace from melting — modder’s custom power solution claims to fix Nvidia 16-pin GPU meltdowns
articles.text:
Quad 8-pin mod protects the $8,500 RTX 5090 you can’t replace from melting — modder’s custom power solution claims to fix Nvidia 16-pin GPU meltdowns
Nvidia’s GeForce RTX 5090, undeniably one of the best graphics cards of our time, vanished overnight without a trace and is now selling for $8,500 on Amazon. In a recent development, Reddit user DallasGrave showcased a custom quad 8-pin power conversion kit designed for the notorious melting 16-pin (12VHPWR) power connector and the later 12V-2x6 revision. This invention, an upgrade over a previous mod, could reduce the risk of power-related meltdowns.
Unlike the endless stream of aftermarket adapters designed solely to prevent 16-pin power meltdowns, DallasGrave's iteration is more like a power-conversion kit. The direct-mount kit sits above the graphics card and uses a custom harness soldered to the graphics card’s PCB power rails. The quad 8-pin power conversion kit bypasses the 16-pin connection and redistributes the massive power draw more evenly across four conventional 8-pin PCIe power connectors.
Each 8-pin PCIe power connector can deliver up to 150W, so all four combined in this custom configuration match the 16-pin connector’s maximum capacity of 600W. However, this configuration addresses concerns with the 16-pin power connector, which channels 50A through a small, tightly packed set of pins. The power-conversion kit instead spreads the load across four 8-pin PCIe power connectors, which are physically larger and allow a wider pin pitch.
While 8-pin PCIe power connectors are not entirely immune to melting or other power-related failures, such incidents are far less common than issues with 16-pin power connectors. The 16-pin power connector is significantly more compact than a single 8-pin power connector and carries 4X the wattage, so it is more prone to higher current density and heat buildup.
According to PCI-SIG specifications, each of the six power pins inside the 16-pin power connector is rated for a maximum current of 9.5A. This means that, in theory, the power connector's total capacity reaches up to 684W or 57A. For example, 600W (50A) requires each power pin to carry about 8.33A, which is already close to the recommended safety limits.
By contrast, a standard 8-pin PCIe power connector contains three power pins. Combining four of these connectors in tandem provides 12 power pins. When distributing a 50A load across 12 pins, each pin carries just 4.17 amps, about half the current per pin of the 16-pin power connector design. This lower current per pin dramatically reduces wire and terminal temperatures and lowers the risk of heat-related damage.
The quad 8-pin power conversion kit tricks the sense pins on the 16-pin power connection into recognizing the full 600W. However, the Redditor claims they have tested the kit for up to 800W with a shunt mod. The beauty of the kit is that users can use it as a standalone power source or alongside the native 16-pin power connector, essentially acting as a parallel load spreader.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
DallasGrave is developing a custom backplate that will enhance the power conversion kit's visual appeal. Notably, it is not limited to the GeForce RTX 5090 or any specific brand. According to the Redditor, they are preparing a range of models for production that cover nearly every variant on the market, including Nvidia’s Founders Edition. However, the creator has not yet revealed key details such as the official release date, pricing, or installation logistics.

Zhiye Liu is a news editor, memory reviewer, and SSD tester at Tom’s Hardware. Although he loves everything that’s hardware, he has a soft spot for CPUs, GPUs, and RAM.

articles.title: Des ingénieurs du MIT mettent au point un dispositif de la taille d'une fenêtre qui exploite l'air pour produire de l'eau potable
articles.text:
Des ingénieurs du MIT mettent au point un dispositif de la taille d'une fenêtre qui exploite l'air pour produire de l'eau potable
Des ingénieurs du MIT ont conçu un collecteur capable d'extraire de l'eau potable directement de l'air, sans électricité ni filtre. Grand comme une fenêtre, le dispositif à base d'hydrogel a été testé avec succès dans la Vallée de la Mort, l'un des endroits les plus arides de la planète. Une piste sérieuse contre l'insécurité hydrique qui touche 2,2 milliards de personnes.
Il y a de l'eau partout autour de vous, même en plein désert. L'atmosphère terrestre en contient des quantités vertigineuses, sous forme de vapeur invisible, jusque dans l'air le plus sec. Le problème n'a jamais été son absence, mais notre incapacité à la saisir sans machines gourmandes en énergie. C'est ce verrou que vient de faire sauter une équipe du Massachusetts Institute of Technology, avec un objet d'une simplicité désarmante.
Une éponge intelligente qui respire jour et nuit
Le cœur du dispositif ressemble à du papier bulle noir. Ce panneau vertical est fait d'un hydrogel, une matière absorbante moulée en un réseau de petits dômes qui gonflent et se dégonflent au fil de la journée. Cette forme, inspirée de l'origami, n'est pas décorative : en multipliant la surface exposée à l'air, elle accélère la capture de l'humidité. Le matériau combine un polymère souple, du chlorure de lithium, un sel qui attire puissamment la vapeur, et de l'encre noire qui transforme le soleil en chaleur.
Le fonctionnement suit un cycle naturel de vingt-quatre heures, sans le moindre branchement. La nuit, quand l'air est le plus humide, le panneau est exposé et l'hydrogel se gorge de vapeur : les dômes se gonflent. Le jour, l'enceinte de verre se referme, le soleil chauffe l'encre noire et fait évaporer l'eau piégée. Cette vapeur vient alors se condenser sur la vitre. Sa face externe est recouverte d'un film spécial qui la maintient plus froide que l'air ambiant, en renvoyant sa chaleur vers l'espace. Les gouttelettes ruissellent enfin vers des tubes de collecte. Aucune pompe, aucune batterie, aucune pièce mobile.
Le test grandeur nature dans la Vallée de la Mort
Pour prouver la robustesse de l'idée, les chercheurs ont choisi le pire endroit possible : Death Valley, en Californie, où l'air peut descendre sous 20 % d'humidité. Pendant une semaine de novembre 2023, un panneau d'un demi-mètre carré y a produit entre 57 et 161 millilitres d'eau par jour, l'équivalent d'un demi à deux tiers de verre. Le système a fonctionné sur une large plage d'humidité, de 21 à 88 %, captant la vapeur nocturne même lors des pics de sécheresse à 18 %.
Surtout, l'eau recueillie est directement potable. C'était le grand défi des hydrogels au sel : ces matériaux ont tendance à relâcher du lithium dans l'eau, la rendant impropre à la consommation. L'équipe a résolu le problème en ajoutant du glycérol, qui verrouille le sel dans la matrice. Résultat, une concentration en lithium inférieure à 0,06 partie par million, sous les seuils de sécurité de l'Organisation mondiale de la santé, sans aucune filtration. Le panneau garde ces performances pendant au moins un an. Ces travaux, publiés dans la revue Nature Water, établissent une référence pour ce type de collecte passive.
Une promesse réelle, mais pas une baguette magique
L'enjeu dépasse la prouesse de laboratoire. Aujourd'hui, 2,2 milliards d'êtres humains n'ont pas accès à une eau potable sûre, souvent dans des régions isolées, sans réseau électrique ni infrastructure. Un dispositif autonome, sans énergie, installable sur une façade, y ouvre une voie précieuse. Les chercheurs estiment qu'un assemblage d'environ huit panneaux couvrirait les besoins vitaux d'un adulte, et prévoient déjà des essais au Maroc et à Singapour, ainsi qu'un hydrogel de nouvelle génération plus rapide.
Reste à garder la tête froide. Plusieurs experts, cités par CNN, mettent en garde contre l'emballement. À ce stade, le débit reste modeste au regard des besoins réels d'un foyer. Le coût de production reste à démontrer, et le passage à grande échelle constitue un défi industriel entier. Ces réserves ne condamnent pas la technologie, elles la ramènent à sa juste place. Non pas la solution unique à la crise mondiale de l'eau, mais un outil décentralisé de plus, particulièrement pertinent là où rien d'autre ne fonctionne. Faire jaillir quelques verres d'eau potable de l'air le plus sec de la planète, sans la moindre prise de courant, restait il y a peu du domaine de la science-fiction. C'est désormais une réalité mesurée sur le terrain.

articles.title: Spektakuläre „Weltraumqualle“: Das steckt wirklich hinter dem SpaceX-Phänomen
articles.text:
Space Jellyfish am Himmel: Die Wahrheit hinter der „Weltraumqualle“
Die Mission SpaceX CRS-35 ist am 13. Oktober um 6:33 Uhr Ortszeit von der Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida gestartet. An Bord der gestarteten Cargo-Dragon-Rakete befinden sich laut dem Kennedy Space Center der Nasa eine Reihe von wissenschaftlichen Geräten, Experimenten und Fracht, die als Nachschub zur Raumstation ISS geliefert werden sollen. Doch die Nachschubmission sorgt derzeit nicht mit ihrem Ziel, sondern mit ihrem Start für breite Aufmerksamkeit.
Wie entsteht der „Space Jellyfish“ am Himmel?
In den sozialen Medien werden unzählige Bilder und Videos gepostet, die einige Zeit nach dem Start aufgenommen wurden. Am Himmel ist dabei ein bläulicher Schimmer zu sehen, der die Form einer Qualle hat. Was zunächst wie ein KI-generierter Fake aussieht, ist ein echtes Phänomen, das unter bestimmten Umständen nach einem Raketenstart auftreten kann.
Der „Space Jellyfish“, der auch als „Jellyfish Ufo“ oder „Rocket Jellyfish“ bezeichnet wird, besteht aus den Abgasen der Rakete, die sich in den höheren Luftschichten sammeln und dort verharren. Das Phänomen wird allerdings nur sichtbar, wenn der Raketenstart in den frühen Morgen- oder späten Abendstunden stattfindet. Genau dann, wenn die Sonne nicht auf die Erde scheint, aber noch den Himmel beleuchtet.
Dadurch trifft das Sonnenlicht auf die Raketenabgase und erleuchtet sie. Da wir auf der Erde im Dunkeln stehen, werden sie für uns sichtbar. Die aktuelle Weltraumqualle von SpaceX ist dabei kein einzelnes Phänomen. Schon seit den 70ern gab es zahlreiche Raketenstarts, die einen „Space Jellyfish“ nach sich gezogen haben. Als das Phänomen noch nicht weitläufig bekannt war, wurden die Sichtungen oftmals als Ufos oder Anzeichen für nukleare Raketenschläge gehalten, wie die Washington Post schon 2017 berichtete.
Für SpaceX ist das Phänomen natürlich eine willkommene Werbung für den Flug zur ISS. Ob die Uhrzeit so gelegt war, dass die Möglichkeit eines „Space Jellyfishs“ erhöht ist, ist nicht bekannt. SpaceX musste den Flug schon zweimal verschieben. Er sollte ursprünglich im November 2026 stattfinden, wurde dann aber aufgrund von Schäden an einem russischen Launch-Pad auf August vorgezogen. So sollte sichergestellt werden, dass die Astronaut:innen auf der ISS ausreichend Nachschub für das kommende Jahr bekommen. Als das Launch-Pad schneller als erwartet repariert werden konnte, wurde der Start wieder nach hinten geschoben.

articles.title: iPhone Duo : le smartphone pliant d’Apple se revend déjà à 5 000 dollars sur eBay
articles.text:
Il n’a même pas encore rejoint les mains de ses premiers acheteurs que l’iPhone Duo s’arrache déjà à prix d’or sur le marché de la revente. Aux États-Unis, deux exemplaires ont été vendus sur eBay pour plusieurs milliers de dollars.
Il aura fallu quelques minutes pour que les premières précommandes de l’iPhone Duo se transforment en opportunité pour certains revendeurs. Repérée par Vadim Yuryev, de la chaîne YouTube Max Tech, une annonce eBay affiche un exemplaire du smartphone pliant vendu 5 000 dollars. Une somme qui dépasse largement le prix demandé par Apple, même pour sa configuration la plus chère. Et ce n’est pas un cas isolé.
Un iPhone Duo revendu 1 800 dollars au-dessus de son prix
Le modèle concerné est un iPhone Duo Night Sky (Ciel nocturne) doté de 2 To de stockage. Aux États-Unis, Apple le vend 3 199 dollars, contre 3 839 euros en France. Sur eBay, il aurait donc trouvé preneur pour 1 800 dollars supplémentaires. Autrement dit, l’acheteur a payé plus de la moitié du prix officiel en plus pour obtenir le smartphone. Mais ce n’est pas tout.
Une deuxième annonce, elle aussi marquée comme vendue, affiche un tarif de 4 400 dollars pour un iPhone Duo Night Sky de 1 To. Commercialisé 3 089 euros en France, son prix officiel américain est de 2 599 dollars. Là encore, l’écart atteint 1 800 dollars.
Ces deux ventes donnent un aperçu des sommes astronomiques que certains acheteurs sont prêts à débourser pour mettre la main sur le premier smartphone pliant d’Apple. En France, la facture est déjà élevée sans passer par la revente : l’iPhone Duo démarre à 2 339 euros pour 256 Go et grimpe jusqu’à 3 839 euros dans sa version de 2 To.
Des livraisons repoussées à l'année prochaine
Pour ceux qui ont manqué l’ouverture des précommandes, recevoir l’iPhone Duo avant la fin d’année semble désormais compromis, y compris dans l’Hexagone. Sur l’Apple Store en ligne, la date de livraison estimée est récemment passée au 25 janvier pour toutes les configurations. Le smartphone est donc indisponible pour une livraison en décembre, du moins selon les délais actuellement affichés par Apple.
Le retrait en magasin, brièvement proposé au lancement des précommandes, n’est plus disponible non plus. Il y a encore quelques heures, la marque à la pomme invitait les clients à vérifier de nouveau cette option à partir du samedi 24 octobre. En France, les acheteurs devront surtout surveiller les disponibilités auprès d’Apple et des revendeurs agréés. Pour l’heure, les délais annoncés ne permettent pas de tirer de conclusion sur les stocks qui seront proposés dans l’Hexagone.
Source : MacRumors

articles.title: Almería tiene todo el sol del mundo para llenar España de energía solar. El problema es que la red no está a su altura
articles.text:
Almería es perfecta para la energía fotovoltaica. Su paisaje árido y sus interminables horas de sol la convierten en un lugar privilegiado para la instalación de este tipo de centrales. Sin embargo, tiene un problema que no tiene que ver con los paneles, y es que no tiene manera de evacuar toda la electricidad que genera. Por eso, aquí la energía, lejos de ser una bendición, es casi un quebradero de cabeza.
Almería tiene el recurso solar que cualquier promotor fotovoltaico querría. La provincia acumula una elevada cantidad de horas de sol al año y unas condiciones especialmente buenas para la generación fotovoltaica. A 30 de junio de 2026, según recoge el Diario de Almería, la provincia cuenta con 1.742,9 MW de potencia renovable instalada. De esa cantidad, 1.220 MW corresponden a la energía fotovoltaica, que ha multiplicado su potencia instalada en apenas cinco años, precisamente por su idoneidad. En 2021, eran 285,9 MW fotovoltaicos, según los datos recogidos por Diario de Almería a partir de la Junta de Andalucía.
Además, actualmente existen importantes proyectos en distintas fases de tramitación, como, por ejemplo, 25 plantas fotovoltaicas que sumarían otros 842 MW, además de parques eólicos y de baterías de almacenamiento independiente.
Potencia instalada no es potencia que se puede inyectar a la red. El sistema eléctrico no tiene una capacidad ilimitada. Para decidir si una instalación puede conectarse, Red Eléctrica lleva a cabo estudios para determinar, entre algunos aspectos, la seguridad y el comportamiento de la red. El resultado de esa investigación establece la capacidad de acceso disponible en cada nudo.
Además, existe otro concepto clave: la evacuación. La electricidad generada tiene que poder circular después por las líneas y subestaciones del sistema sin superar las restricciones técnicas existentes, pero no significa que una planta tenga garantizada la evacuación de toda su producción en todo momento. Por el contrario, puede darse la situación de que existan restricciones adicionales a tiempo real. Es decir, un parque solar puede tener 100 MW de paneles, pero eso no significa que la red tenga necesariamente un hueco de 100 MW para recibirlos.
¿Cuál es el problema? Almería podría convertirse en toda una potencia solar, pero (nunca mejor dicho) no es oro todo lo que reluce y su capacidad solar no está creciendo al mismo ritmo que otras provincias andaluzas, como Jaén o Sevilla. Según explica el delegado de Economía, Hacienda y Fondos Europeos de la Junta en Almería, Guillermo Casquet, a Diario de Almería, esto se debe a la capacidad de evacuación disponible.
En las horas donde hay más recurso solar, los parques almerienses producen más electricidad de la que la red puede absorber. Para entender esto, hay que imaginar las redes de alta tensión como un entramado de carreteras por donde se transporta la electricidad hasta el sistema eléctrico: si estas redes están limitadas es como si la carretera tuviese menos carriles que los necesarios para esa cantidad de tráfico. Para evitar esa congestión, el operador del sistema, como explica La Voz de Almería, se ve obligado a reducir la producción de las centrales (lo que se conoce como curtailment) para garantizar así la estabilidad del suministro y no comprometer su seguridad.
Tabernas es uno de los ejemplos más extremos. Según El Periódico de la Energía, que cita datos de Optimize Energy, la localidad almeriense de Tabernas sería un buen ejemplo de este fenómeno. Para este medio, haber desarrollado energía solar fotovoltaica en esta zona ha sido una «absoluta ruina», puesto que pierde casi la mitad de la energía que genera. Con una subestación de 400 kV que atiende a varias plantas fotovoltaicas, «la física no da más de sí» y, según los datos, se ha alcanzado un porcentaje de curtailment de más del 41% solamente en ese nudo.
De ahí que la planificación de la red para los próximos años vaya a ser fundamental. Sin embargo, Guillermo Casquet, en sus declaraciones a Diario de Almería, tilda los planes actuales de «insuficientes» y lamenta que la provincia no esté recibiendo una inversión a la altura de sus posibilidades como potencia renovable.

articles.title: MOZA AY210 Force Feedback Base and MFY Yoke review: Taking flight sim immersion to the next level
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The MOZA AY210 Force Feedback Base and MFY Yoke Bundle delivers an incredible flight sim experience, combining force feedback, exceptional build quality, and precise control. However, the elevator can feel somewhat “sticky” without the proper settings and its premium price makes it a significant investment.
Reasons to buy
- + High level of precision
- + Exceptional build quality
- + Force feedback
- + Autopilot following
Reasons to avoid
- - Sticky along the elevator axis without the proper settings
- - Pricing
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Over the past several years, MOZA Racing has become one of the most recognizable names in sim racing, earning a reputation for producing high-quality racing wheels and peripherals. Founded in 2012 by a group of automotive engineers and sim racing enthusiasts, the company initially focused on manufacturing and selling videography equipment before entering the sim-racing market.
More recently, MOZA has expanded into the world of flight simulation, bringing the same focus on build quality and performance that has made its racing products so popular. Today, we’re taking a look at the MOZA AY210 Force Feedback Base and MFY Yoke. We’ll be putting both products through their paces in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, testing them across a variety of challenging flight scenarios to see how they perform in the cockpit.
Inside the Box

While you can purchase the base and the yoke separately, they also come in a bundle. With the bundle, you get both the yoke and the base in the box, along with a toolkit and user manual. The base comes with a power cable and a USB Type A to Type B cable.
MOZA also sent us a couple of table clamps for the yoke to secure it to our test setup. The clamps are sold separately.

Customization
The base and yoke feature several programmable buttons and switches, but the real depth of customization comes from MOZA Cockpit Software. The software provides an impressive range of options for fine-tuning the yoke to your preferences. You can adjust individual settings to create your ideal feel, or choose from one of MOZA’s presets or community-created profiles.
Build Quality
The base is constructed from aluminum alloy, giving it a sturdy, durable, and premium feel. An aluminum quick-release mechanism allows you to swap yokes quickly while keeping them securely attached.
Under the hood, the AY210 is powered by a 280 MHz processor and features a 15-bit high-resolution magnetic encoder. This is designed to provide precise and responsive inputs across the full range of motion, whether you’re making small, delicate adjustments or larger, more aggressive inputs. Combined with MOZA’s proprietary active force-feedback system, the AY210 is designed to deliver a high level of control while adding another layer of immersion to the flight experience.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The MFY Yoke features a premium build made from high-quality synthetic engineering thermoplastic and ergonomic design that closely replicates the feel of a yoke found in a real commercial aircraft.
How Does it Feel?
The star of the show is undoubtedly the force feedback. With up to 9 Nm of torque and 210 N of push force, the system adds a level of immersion that simply isn’t possible with conventional yokes that lack force feedback.
When flying the PMDG 737, the yoke gives the aircraft a noticeably heavier feel through the control column, closely mimicking what we experienced in a 737 simulator. As airspeed increases, the yoke becomes progressively harder to deflect in both pitch and roll, accurately reflecting the aerodynamic forces acting on the aircraft.
But the force feedback goes far beyond simply simulating control forces. You can feel the vibrations from the engines, as well as the movement of the flaps and spoilers. After takeoff, the yoke conveys the increasing resistance of the airflow as the aircraft accelerates. Approaching a stall during a climb produces a noticeable buffet through the controls, while landing provides feedback as the wheels make contact with the runway.
The AY210 also replicates the movement of the aircraft's controls when the autopilot is engaged, with the yoke moving under the control of the autopilot servos.
All of these effects work together to create a remarkably convincing connection between the aircraft and the controls. It’s a level of immersion that most other yokes simply cannot replicate.
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 Testing
We tested the AY210 Force Feedback Base and MFY Yoke in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 primarily using the PMDG 737-800. While the iFly 737 MAX is a great addon with a superb flight model, especially in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020, it is not yet natively built for MSFS 2024. As such, it does not handle wind and turbulence effects entirely well in MSFS 2024. We wanted to stick with MSFS 2024 because of its more realistic flight dynamics. We also tested the yoke with the PMDG 777. For our tests, we used the latest 737 NG and 777 profiles from Tonyaviation on Flightsim.to. Tony is a real-life pilot with experience in the 737 and 787. The 787 and 777 share many of the same flight characteristics.
We tested the base and yoke in three different scenarios:
- Basic maneuvering. Flying at 5,000 feet, we performed gentle turns and pitch changes to evaluate the precision of the base during small, accurate control inputs.
- Turbulent approach. We performed an approach into Las Vegas under hot, windy conditions with strong updrafts and downdrafts. This scenario required larger, more frequent control inputs to assess how the base handles turbulence and rapid corrections.
- Curved approach. Finally, we flew the RNAV Visual approach to Runway 1R at San Francisco International Airport. This approach is available in MSFS 2024 if you use the Navigraph database, but it is missing the RF leg between the waypoints KLAUS and SQIRL, so we added it to the navigation database of the PMDG 737 and 777 ourselves. The procedure features a sweeping right-hand arc that continues until roughly one mile from the runway threshold, requiring the aircraft to remain in a turn at very low altitude. The approach demands precise tracking of the flight path while also requiring a smooth, accurate transition to the runway centerline after the final waypoint. This scenario tested both the precision and responsiveness of the AY210 Base.
Basic Maneuvering
Basic maneuvering feels precise and smooth with the right settings. That last part is important, however, because the AY210 does not necessarily deliver this experience out of the box. Based on our previous experience with a 737 simulator, even with significant pitch input, the control column should maintain a smooth and consistent feel throughout its movement. With the AY210, we found that the motion could feel less natural and “sticky” unless Pitch Friction Correction was enabled in the MOZA Cockpit Software. Fortunately, this setting significantly improves the feel, giving the control column a response that is much closer to what we experienced in a 737 simulator.The 280 MHz processor and 15-bit high-resolution magnetic encoder also contribute to the AY210’s precise and responsive inputs. We were able to make accurate turns and precisely set our desired descent rate, with even small control inputs translating smoothly and predictably into the simulator.
Turbulent Approach
Here, we perform our usual turbulent approach, landing in Las Vegas during the summer. The combination of extreme heat, strong winds, and thermals along the approach path can create significant turbulence, making for a much less stable approach. Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is able to replicate these conditions through its Live Weather system, providing a challenging environment for testing the AY210.
The level of immersion provided by the AY210 is simply incredible. Through the force feedback system, you can feel the effects of wind and turbulence directly through the yoke, rather than relying solely on visual cues or the aircraft’s instruments. This provides useful feedback that helps you anticipate and make the necessary control corrections. The AY210 handled these conditions exceptionally well, accurately conveying the changing forces throughout the approach and giving us a much better sense of how the aircraft was responding.
Curved Approach
The RNAV Visual approach to Runway 1R at San Francisco International Airport contains an RF leg between the final two waypoints – KLAUS and SQIRL – which is a sweeping right-hand arc. The AY210 was responsive and precise throughout, allowing us to follow the arc all the way to SQIRL, at which point we were able to accurately align with runway 1R and perform a smooth landing.
By comparison, the Thrustmaster TCA Boeing Yoke felt noticeably jerkier throughout the approach. The two products are also in completely different price tiers, so this is not necessarily a direct or entirely fair comparison. However, the TCA Boeing Yoke is a popular choice among simmers flying Boeing aircraft in Microsoft Flight Simulator, making it a useful reference point. The difference was immediately noticeable, and the AY210’s ability to provide smoother, more natural control while conveying the effects of turbulence is a clear example of what you gain from its more premium design and force feedback system.
Bottom Line
The MOZA AY210 Force Feedback Yoke Base delivers one of the most immersive experiences available in desktop flight simulation. It comes at a premium price, but after spending time with the AY210, it is genuinely difficult to go back to a yoke without force feedback. The combination of realistic feedback, precise control, and the level of detail conveyed through the yoke adds an entirely new dimension to the flying experience.
It is not without its flaws. Some of the force feedback effects could be stronger, while the control column can feel slightly unnatural and “sticky” out of the box. Fortunately, both issues can be addressed to some extent through the extensive customization options in MOZA Cockpit Software.
Overall, the AY210 is an impressive piece of hardware. For those willing to pay the premium, its force feedback and overall level of immersion make it a compelling upgrade for any serious home cockpit.
Dan Mateescu is a PC enthusiast with many years of experience benchmarking PC hardware. In 2021, he started his own YouTube channel called 'Compusemble' where he benchmarks hardware in video games and the latest tech demos.

articles.title: ASUS Makes Its First Intel Arc Card, a 32 GB Arc Pro B70 Under the UGen AI Brand
articles.text:
Saturday, October 17th 2026
ASUS Makes Its First Intel Arc Card, a 32 GB Arc Pro B70 Under the UGen AI Brand
ASUS has listed the UGen Arc Pro B70 32 GB on its website, which makes it the company's first Intel Arc graphics card. ASUS sat out both the Alchemist and Battlemage consumer generations, and its last Intel discrete card was the passively cooled Iris Xe DG1-4G from 2021. Interestingly, ASUS files it under its UGen AI accelerator lineup rather than ProArt, putting it in the same family as the UGen300 USB AI accelerator the company showed at CES 2026. ASUS hasn't announced pricing or a release date yet. Intel launched the Arc Pro B70 at $949 back in March, though US retail listings now seem to sit closer to $1,300.
The ASUS card uses the full "Big Battlemage" BMG-G31 die with 32 Xe2 cores, 256 XMX engines, and 32 GB of GDDR6 ECC memory on a 256-bit bus for 608 GB/s of bandwidth. ASUS rates it at a 2,800 MHz boost clock, up to 367 INT8 TOPS, and a 290 W board power, which is the top of Intel's 160 to 290 W range for the B70 (the reference default is 230 W). Cooling comes from a dual-slot blower, and ASUS says four cards can be paired for 128 GB of combined VRAM, enough for models with up to 120 billion parameters according to the company. ASUS also joins ASRock, Sparkle, and Maxsun, which already have their own B70 models, so pricing will likely decide how well the UGen version does.

articles.title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Replit, the AI coding platform that has become a favorite of startup founders and developers, is no longer working with Anthropic, the company’s CEO and co-founder Amjad Masad said Thursday while onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt.
Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer partnering with Anthropic.
“I think ChatGPT is better now,” Masad said, adding that the company uses an internal benchmark to help assess metrics like performance. “We publish a public benchmark as well, and consistently, Sol and Astra perform better on building vibe-coded applications from scratch. It was a decision based on both cost, partnership, and performance. And for all these reasons, we just felt like they were a better partner for now.”
It seems, however, that Anthropic hasn’t been completely cut out of Replit, which sells a cloud-based software development platform where users can develop and deploy apps directly from inside their browser.
After Disrupt, Masad clarified that customers can still access Anthropic models on the platform, but that OpenAI’s ChatGPT is now the default. This shift could significantly reduce Replit’s spend with Anthropic since most customers stick with the default rather than selecting a model themselves.
Prior to striking a deal with OpenAI, Replit relied on Anthropic’s Claude models to run its platform. That partnership was said to have helped the company grow its revenue significantly, and Masad noted on stage that Replit had been, until recently, a top-five customer of Anthropic’s.
“Replit remains model agnostic,” Masad told TechCrunch over the weekend. “Our users can choose Anthropic’s Claude or other supported models…OpenAI is now our preferred partner for powering Replit Agent, based on performance, economics, and the strength of our partnership.”
Masad’s comments on stage were rejected by insiders familiar with the partnership between the Anthropic and Replit, however. One person familiar, who asked not to be named, said the partnership was still in place.
There is evidence on the company’s website, blog posts, and social media posts that Replit was promoting Anthropic products as recently as a few weeks ago. For instance, a blog post in late September cites Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 and Claude Fable 5.1 as models running in Replit Agent’s production environment. Around the same time, one of Replit’s product employees posted on X about using Anthropic’s flagship model Opus 5.5 and promoting its capabilities.
Masad also shared insights about the company’s growth while onstage at Disrupt, noting that enterprise is starting to provide a larger slice of revenue.
“We’re not sharing ARR numbers just yet, but in terms of growth, like, I would say, enterprise was like 2% of revenue last year,” Masad said. “This year, I would say like 15% of our revenue is enterprise contracts, and more than 50% of our revenue is B2B.”
Backstage, Masad told TechCrunch that he expects more than half of Replit’s revenue to come from enterprise and government customers in 2027.
Masad also commented on the necessity for good AI safety measures.
“In the same way that us humans need a certain environment to work — you need a nice office, maybe nice good food in the office, air-conditioning, computer — agents need a habitat for them to exist and do good work,” he said. “So that habitat has good orchestration, good error recovery, good safety and security and sandboxing, good networking, good identity and authorization. And once you figure all of that out, then you can deploy AI safely.”
This article was originally published on October 16 at 2:22 pm PT. It has been updated to include more context around Replit’s partnerships with Anthropic and OpenAI. Its title has been updated, as well.

articles.title: Lancé à 1299€, le robot laveur Dreame L50 Pro Ultra tombe à 599€ chez Darty
articles.text:
Lancé à 1 299 € en février 2025, le Dreame L50 Pro Ultra s’affiche à 599 € sur Darty, vendu par Dreame Tech sur la place de marché de l’enseigne. Reste à savoir pour quel logement ce robot laveur à station automatique est un bon calcul, et où il fait des concessions.
Le Dreame L50 Pro Ultra réunit une station qui vide, lave et sèche, un capteur laser escamotable et deux bras extensibles. Il est proposé à 599 € au lieu de 1 099 € sur Darty, soit 500 € de moins que son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours chez ce marchand, le même tarif que l’offre la moins chère relevée ce matin chez Cdiscount.
Précision : il est vendu et expédié par Dreame Tech sur la place de marché, pas par Darty. L’offre parle d’abord aux foyers à sols durs qui veulent déléguer aspiration et serpillière, moins aux intérieurs couverts de tapis épais.
Le Dreame L50 Pro Ultra passe à 599 € au lieu de 1 099 € sur Darty, vendu et expédié par Dreame Tech.
Pourquoi choisir le Dreame L50 Pro Ultra ?
- Une station qui entretient le robot : la base PowerDock vide le bac dans un sac de 3,2 litres prévu pour tenir jusqu’à 100 jours, lave les serpillières à l’eau chaude à 75 °C puis les sèche à l’air chaud. Restent les réservoirs et le sac à gérer.
- Des bras qui vont chercher les bords : la technologie Dual Flex Arm déploie la brosse latérale et la serpillière vers les plinthes et les angles, là où un robot rond ne passe pas.
- Un robot qui se faufile et franchit : son capteur laser se rétracte pour ramener sa hauteur à 8,95 cm sous les meubles bas, et le système EasyLeap lui fait passer des seuils jusqu’à 4 cm.
Sols durs, poils d’animaux et meubles bas : son terrain de jeu
Avec 19 500 Pa d’aspiration annoncés et une brosse double HyperStream conçue pour ne pas s’emmêler, le L50 Pro Ultra vise les cheveux longs et les poils d’animaux. Test-Achats, qui l’a mesuré en laboratoire, lui reconnaît une bonne efficacité sur sols durs, carrelage comme parquet, sur les peluches comme sur les miettes. Son capteur DToF et son éclairage l’aident à identifier plus de 180 types d’objets, câbles et déjections animales compris, ce qui limite le rangement préalable.
Le profil le plus cohérent : un foyer avec un chien ou un chat, des sols durs et peu d’envie d’entretenir la machine elle-même. Les serpillières se relèvent lorsque le robot détecte un tapis, ce qui suffit pour des poils courts. En revanche, Vanden Borre le déclare non compatible avec les tapis à poils longs : un intérieur couvert de moquette épaisse ne profitera pas de son lavage. Nous ne l’avons pas encore testé, et cet avis s’appuie donc sur sa fiche technique et sur les mesures publiées par Test-Achats.
Serpillières rotatives contre rouleau : où il se situe
Le L50 Pro Ultra lave avec deux serpillières rotatives, quand plusieurs modèles retenus dans notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs robots misent sur un rouleau serpillière, comme le Dreame Aqua10 Ultra Roller Complete, notre recommandation toutes catégories. Pour le lavage jusque dans les coins, ce guide distingue le Dreame X60 Pro Ultra Complete et sa serpillière extensible, un principe que le L50 Pro Ultra reprend avec ses bras Dual Flex ARM. À 599 €, il s’adresse à ceux qui veulent une station complète pour moins de la moitié de son prix de lancement.
✅ Les points forts
- Station qui vide le bac, lave les serpillières à 75 °C et les sèche
- Bras extensibles pour les plinthes et les angles
- Capteur laser rétractable, 8,95 cm de haut sous les meubles
- Brosse double conçue contre l’enroulement des cheveux et des poils
- 500 € sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours chez Darty
❌ Les limites
- Non adapté aux tapis à poils longs
- Sacs à poussière à racheter pour la station
- Station encombrante : près de 59 cm de haut pour 46 cm de profondeur
- Qualité globale jugée seulement raisonnable par Test-Achats
Avant de valider le Dreame L50 Pro Ultra à 599 €, vérifiez sur la fiche Darty que Dreame Tech en est toujours le vendeur.
À 599 €, le Dreame L50 Pro Ultra coûte moins de la moitié de son prix de lancement et réunit l’essentiel d’un robot laveur autonome : vidage automatique, serpillières lavées à l’eau chaude puis séchées, bras qui atteignent les bords. Pour un foyer à sols durs avec un animal, c’est une façon concrète de confier au robot la corvée de serpillière. Les mesures de Test-Achats sur sols durs vont dans ce sens.
Si votre intérieur compte surtout des tapis épais, ou si la place manque pour une station de près de 60 cm de haut, mieux vaut regarder ailleurs. Si vous hésitez avec un modèle à rouleau, notre guide aide à trancher selon vos sols. Et puisque l’offre passe par un vendeur de la place de marché, un coup d’œil à la garantie et aux conditions de retour avant de payer reste un bon réflexe.

articles.title: Recht bei Reklamationen: So wehren Sie sich gegen die „Hersteller-Ausrede“ der Händler
articles.text:
Reklamation abgelehnt? So wehrst du dich gegen Händler-Ausreden
Es ist ein Klassiker im Online- und stationären Handel: Wer ein defektes Gerät beim Händler reklamiert, bekommt oftmals gesagt, dass er sich doch bitte direkt an den Hersteller wenden möge, weil man ihm dort schneller helfen könne und man das Gerät ja ohnehin einschicken würde. Doch der Reparaturservice des Herstellers, der sich um solche Probleme kümmern soll, ist in diesem Fall nicht die erste Anlaufstelle, wie ein neues Urteil zeigt.
Klar, für den Händler ist es praktisch, wenn sich die Kund:innen mit dem Service herumärgern müssen, doch für diese bedeutet es oftmals zusätzlichen Aufwand. Es ist aber vor allem rechtlich problematisch, wenn damit die Verantwortung für die gesetzliche Gewährleistung auf den Hersteller abgeschoben werden soll.
Mediamarkt wurde nun seitens des Landgerichts Ingolstadt dieses Vorgehen untersagt. Im Verfahren des Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverbands (vzbv) gegen die MMS E-Commerce GmbH – das ist die Onlinetochter besagter Elektronikmarktkette – entschieden die Richter, dass die Aufforderung gegenüber den Kund:innen, Gewährleistungsansprüche direkt beim Hersteller geltend zu machen, irreführend ist. Das Urteil vom 24. Juli 2026 (Az. 1 HK O 1352/25) wurde in der vergangenen Woche veröffentlicht und ist noch nicht rechtskräftig.
Ein lästig piepsender Kühlschrank
Im konkreten Fall ging es um eine Kühl-Gefrier-Kombination. Die hatte der Kunde gut ein Jahr davor im Mediamarkt-Onlineshop erworben. Das Gerät entwickelte im Laufe der Zeit aber die unangenehme Eigenart, dass der Alarm, der normalerweise vor einer zu lange geöffneten Tür warnt, auch bei geschlossener Tür ausgelöst wurde.
Als sich das nicht mehr abschalten ließ und zu lästig wurde, wandte sich der Kunde daher an Mediamarkt, um im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Gewährleistung eine Lösung zu finden. Mediamarkt verwies ihn daraufhin an den Vor-Ort-Reparaturservice des Herstellers und forderte ihn auf, sich zur Durchsetzung seiner Garantie- beziehungsweise Gewährleistungsansprüche mit diesem direkt auseinanderzusetzen. Die Kontaktdaten finde er im Gerätehandbuch.
Das Gericht befand, die Antwort erwecke den Eindruck, Mediamarkt sei für die Reklamation nicht zuständig. Denn tatsächlich steht bei gesetzlichen Gewährleistungsansprüchen immer zunächst der Verkäufer als Vertragspartner in der Pflicht. Er ist – und darin wurde die Rechtslage bestätigt – Ansprechpartner für den Käufer oder die Käuferin. Dass sich der Kunde in diesem Fall nicht abwimmeln ließ und weiterhin auf eine Abwicklung über Mediamarkt bestand, änderte für das Gericht nichts an der irreführenden Aussage des Unternehmens.
Was das Urteil für den Handel bedeutet
Die Entscheidung betrifft einmal mehr die grundsätzliche Frage im E-Commerce (ebenso wie im Handel vor Ort), wer für die Bearbeitung einer Reklamation verantwortlich ist. Zwar können die Händler durchaus den Hersteller oder einen weiteren externen Dienstleister mit einer Reparatur beauftragen. Allerdings lässt sich daraus nicht ableiten, dass sie ihre gesetzlichen Verpflichtungen gegenüber den Käufern auf diese Unternehmen übertragen könnten.
Doch wie immer geht’s dabei um den Unterschied zwischen Gewährleistung und Garantie. Während sich die gesetzliche Gewährleistung grundsätzlich gegen den Verkäufer richtet und bei Neuwaren im Verbrauchsgüterbereich in aller Regel zwei Jahre beträgt, ist eine zusätzliche Herstellergarantie eine freiwillig eingeräumte Leistung, deren Bedingungen sich nach der jeweiligen Garantieerklärung richten. Entscheidend wäre hier lediglich noch die Beweislastumkehr, die nach einem Jahr in Kraft tritt, aber die ist hier nicht Gegenstand des Falls gewesen.
Das bedeutet, dass Kunden innerhalb der gesetzlichen Voraussetzungen vom Händler Nacherfüllung verlangen können, also eine Reparatur oder Ersatzlieferung. Allerdings kann der Verkäufer die gewählte Form unter bestimmten gesetzlichen Voraussetzungen verweigern. Er darf aber nicht pauschal seine Zuständigkeit abstreiten. Insofern ist das Urteil keine Neuregelung, sondern eher eine Erinnerung an bestehende Pflichten.
Es geht dabei aber vor allem auch um die klaren Hinweise an den Kunden: Reklamationsprozesse, automatisierte Serviceantworten und Hinweise auf Herstellerservices müssen deutlich machen, dass die gesetzlichen Ansprüche gegenüber dem Verkäufer oder der Verkäuferin bestehen bleiben.
Immerhin erklärte eine Mediamarkt-Sprecherin gegenüber Medienvertretern, man respektiere die Entscheidung des Landgerichts und arbeite an der adäquaten Umsetzung. Auf seiner Hilfeseite empfiehlt Mediamarkt bei defekten Großgeräten weiterhin die direkte Kontaktaufnahme mit dem Hersteller und begründet das damit, dass dieser Weg in der Regel schneller sei. Ein solcher Hinweis muss nicht grundsätzlich unzulässig sein, sollte aber im Hinblick auf die nächsten Maßnahmen der Verbraucherschützer nicht ohne Weiteres da stehen. Entscheidend ist nämlich, dass nicht der Eindruck entsteht, Kunden müssten ihre Gewährleistungsrechte beim Hersteller statt beim Händler geltend machen.
Für kleinere Onlinehändler ein guter Anlass, die eigene Reklamationsseite einmal durchzugehen: Steht da irgendwo, dass sich Kund:innen an den Hersteller wenden sollen, würde ich das umformulieren. Besser ist ein klarer Ablauf mit Formular und Rücksendeetikett, und der Kontakt zum Hersteller als freiwillige Zusatzoption. Das spart nicht nur Ärger mit Abmahnungen, sondern bringt auch bessere Bewertungen, weil der Service beim Shop bleibt. Gerade auf Shopify lässt sich so ein Retourenprozess mit ein paar Apps recht schnell aufsetzen.

articles.title: Un sismógrafo casero por 100 dólares: esta joven de 17 años ha logrado lo que parecía imposible frente a los terremotos
articles.text:
Durante el confinamiento, hay quien se puso a hacer pan, a otra gente le dio por ponerse en forma en casa y una estudiante de un instituto de California aprovechó su tiempo libre para hacer un sismógrafo que ella misma había diseñado, soldado y programado. Algunos detalles más de su instrumento: tenía el tamaño de un cubo de Rubik y una atractiva carcasa de acrílico transparente, fabricarlo le costó menos de 100 dólares y lo más interesante de todo: funcionaba.
El invento. El día después de montarlo hubo un terremoto en Los Ángeles y la onda que dibujó su sismógrafo casero coincidía con la de una estación del Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos (USGS). A grandes rasgos, su sismógrafo casero integra un geófono que detecta el movimiento del suelo y después, su electrónica y software convierten esa señal en una onda digital. Si el sismo supera el umbral fijado, el dispositivo hace sonar una alarma, puede mandar un SMS y se controla desde el móvil. Además, es capaz de almacenar hasta cuatro años de registros, como profundiza Science Blog.
Un sismógrafo cualitativo. De hecho, fue capaz de detectar todos los terremotos de magnitud superior a 3,0 en torno a Los Ángeles entre septiembre de 2020 y abril de 2021. La joven en cuestión se llama Vivien He y en 2021 acudió a una reunión de la Sociedad Sismológica de América a enseñar su dispositivo.
El problema a resolver. Los sistemas de alerta temprana no predicen terremotos, solo avisan cuando uno ya ha empezado. Sin ánimo de profundizar demasiado, cuando un terremoto se produce, genera dos tipos de onda: las P que son las que antes llegan y las S, que llegan después y son las más dañinas. Pues bien, este tipo de sistemas detectan las P y avisan antes de que lleguen las S. Un ejemplo: según el USGS, el ShakeAlert de la costa oeste de EEUU da un margen de entre unos pocos segundos y decenas de segundos. Obviamente, en el epicentro no hay mucho que hacer.
Vivien He vio un hueco justo ahí, entre sistemas científicos más caros, como ShakeAlert, y una opción pensada para particulares. ¿El resultado? Un aparato barato y diseñado para el consumidor.
El silencio del COVID-19. Con la actividad humana diaria (el transporte, las fábricas y hasta nuestro caminar) producimos vibraciones que los sismómetros detectan: es el “ruido sísmico”. En 2020, buena parte de esa actividad se paró y se notó hubo hasta un 50% menos. Esa calma permitió detectar señales débiles del subsuelo que normalmente quedan tapadas. Ese estudio fue el punto de partida de He. "Me pregunté si podía medirlo desde mi propia casa". Y de ahí evolucionó hasta la alerta temprana de terremotos.
Cómo lo hizo. Como cuenta en EOS, la publicación de la American Geophysical Union, no tenía formación previa en electrónica ni programación, así que aprendió Python por su cuenta y leyó papers sobre detección de terremotos. De hecho, ella resume el proceso en una frase: ella "googleaba todo". Friendly reminder de que estamos hablando de 2020, dos años antes del lanzamiento de ChatGPT y el boom de la IA.
